definition_zh: 精算师；保险精算师
definition_en: a person whose job is to calculate insurance risks and premiums using statistics
core_image: 一堆保单和表格前，有人正在算未来会赔多少钱
scene: 保险公司年底盘点，办公室里表格摞得半人高，有人还在核对新产品的费率。The actuary recalculated the premiums for the new policy.
sceneCN: 这里 actuary 是「精算师」（第 1 个义项：用统计方法计算保险风险与保费的专业人员）；句意为精算师重新核算了新保单的保费。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加形容词后缀构成，义为「精算的；保险精算的」
由本词构成的复合说法，义为「精算学」

senses.title: Insurance risk professional
senses.definition: a professional who computes insurance risks, premiums, and reserves with statistics
senses.definitionCN: 用统计方法计算保险风险、保费与准备金的专业人员
senses.example: The actuary recalculated the premiums for the new policy.
senses.exampleCN: 精算师重新核算了新保单的保费。
senses.why: Latin actuarius was a clerk who recorded accounts; the modern actuary still keeps the accounts of future risk.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 actuarius 是记录账目的书记员；现代精算师仍在为未来的风险记账。

senses.title: Pension and fund adviser
senses.titleCN: 养老金与基金测算顾问
senses.definition: an expert who evaluates pension schemes and investment funds for long-term solvency
senses.definitionCN: 评估养老金计划与投资基金长期偿付能力的专家
senses.example: The firm's actuary advised closing the underfunded pension plan.
senses.exampleCN: 公司的精算师建议关闭资金不足的养老金计划。
senses.why: The same arithmetic of future risk extends beyond insurance to any fund that must not run dry.
senses.whyCN: 同一套未来风险的算术延伸到保险之外，用于任何不能坐吃山空的基金。

intro.en: Actuary goes back to Latin actuarius, 'a clerk of accounts', from actus, 'a doing, a record of proceedings'.
intro.cn: actuary 溯源自拉丁语 actuarius（记账书记员），来自 actus（行为、事务记录）。

items.en: The reconstructed root *ag- meant 'to drive, to do'.
items.cn: 重构词根 *ag- 意为「驱动、做」。

items.en: actus meant 'a doing, an official record'; actuarius was a keeper of such records.
items.cn: actus 意为「行为、公务记录」；actuarius 是保管这类记录的人。

items.en: English actuary first named a clerk of the law courts.
items.cn: 英语 actuary 最初指法院的书记员。

items.en: Insurance companies borrowed the title for their risk calculators.
items.cn: 保险公司借用这个头衔称呼风险计算人员。

items.en: Actuary is now a profession of statistics, finance, and insurance.
items.cn: 如今精算师是一个融合统计、金融与保险的职业。

note.en: The first group gathers words from the Latin agere family; the second gathers finance and risk professions.
note.cn: 第一组收来自拉丁语 agere 词族的词；第二组收金融与风险行业的职业名称。

entries.definition: The adjective for actuary-related calculation.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「精算的」。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'real, existing in fact'; from the same agere family, only spelling near.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「实际的」；与 actuary 同源，词义已分道。

entries.definition: A common phrase for statistical life-expectancy tables.
entries.definitionCN: 短语，义为「精算表」，记录预期寿命等统计数据的表格。

entries.definition: A person or company that takes on insurance risk.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「承保人」，承担保险风险的一方。

entries.definition: An expert in statistical methods.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「统计学家」。

entries.definition: A professional who examines accounts.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「审计员」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the clerk-of-accounts root and the premium scene; the abstract hooks picture tables that see the future.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「记账书记员」词根与保费场景；抽象记忆点想象能看见未来的表格。

normal.en: Actuary comes from actuarius, a Latin clerk of accounts.
normal.cn: actuary 来自拉丁语 actuarius，记账书记员。

normal.en: Actuarial tables list life expectancy for pricing.
normal.cn: 精算表列出预期寿命，用于定价。

normal.en: The plural changes y to i: actuaries.

normal.en: Actuarial science is the degree that trains actuaries.
normal.cn: 精算学是培养精算师的学位。

normal.en: Actual shares the Latin family but means 'real'.
normal.cn: actual 同属拉丁词族，但意为「实际的」。

abstract.en: Picture a clerk adding columns that reach into the future.
abstract.cn: 想象书记员算着一列列伸向未来的数字。

abstract.en: Picture a life table where every age has a price.
abstract.cn: 想象一张每个年龄都标着价格的寿命表。

abstract.en: Picture a dam keeper measuring tomorrow's rain.
abstract.cn: 想象守坝人在测算明天的降雨。

examples.en: The actuary recalculated the premiums for the new policy.
examples.cn: 精算师重新核算了新保单的保费。

examples.en: Skilled actuaries are in high demand at insurance firms.
examples.cn: 保险公司对熟练的精算师需求很大。

examples.en: The actuary warned that the fund would run out in twenty years.
examples.cn: 精算师警告该基金二十年内会耗尽。

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from calculating insurance risks, to evaluating pensions and funds.

core.cn: 核心意象：账目伸向未来的记账书记员

branches.en: The professional who prices insurance risk.
branches.cn: 为保险风险定价的专业人员。

branches.en: The adviser who tests whether a fund can last.
branches.cn: 检验基金能否长期维系的顾问。

branches.en: Both senses turn statistics into money decisions.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把统计变成金钱决策。

branches.en: The old clerk of records survives in both roles.

intro.cn: 这个词带着拉丁语「记录」词根 act- 与施动词尾 -uary，词族还产出 actual 与 act。

latinIntro.en: Latin actus and actuarius are the direct ancestors recorded here.
latinIntro.cn: 这里记录的拉丁语 actus 与 actuarius 是直接祖先。

definition_zh: 使动作；开动（机器）；驱使（人行动）
definition_en: to make a machine work, or to cause someone to act in a certain way
core_image: 按下开关，齿轮咔哒一声转起来
scene: 老式电梯要通电了，工人把手柄一扳，缆绳立刻绷紧。A lever actuates the safety brake when the cable snaps.
sceneCN: 这里 actuate 是「使动作、触发」（第 1 个义项：让机械装置开始工作）；句意为缆绳断裂时连杆会触发安全制动。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「启动；驱动」
由本词加施动后缀构成，义为「执行器；促动器」

senses.title: To set a mechanism in motion
senses.definition: to put a machine or device into action
senses.definitionCN: 让机器或装置开始运作
senses.example: A lever actuates the safety brake when the cable snaps.
senses.exampleCN: 缆绳断裂时连杆会触发安全制动。
senses.why: Latin agere meant 'to drive'; actuate is to drive a thing into doing its work.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 agere 意为「驱动」；actuate 就是把一件东西驱入它的工作状态。

senses.title: To motivate a person to act
senses.definition: to be the inner cause of someone's behaviour
senses.definitionCN: 成为某人行为的内在动因
senses.example: She was actuated by loyalty, not by hope of reward.
senses.exampleCN: 驱使她的是忠诚，而不是报酬的希望。
senses.why: The same driving force applied to a person becomes motive; the mind is the machine being switched on.
senses.whyCN: 同一股驱动力作用到人身上就成了动机；心智就是那台被按下开关的机器。

intro.en: Actuate joins Latin actus, 'a doing', with the verb ending -ate, 'to make'.
intro.cn: actuate 把拉丁语 actus（行为）与动词词尾 -ate（使）结合。

items.en: The reconstructed root *ag- meant 'to drive, to do'.
items.cn: 重构词根 *ag- 意为「驱动、做」。

items.en: actus meant 'a doing, a driving'.
items.cn: actus 意为「行为、驱动」。

items.en: actuare meant 'to put into action'.
items.cn: actuare 意为「使付诸行动」。

items.en: English actuate was first used of machines and springs.
items.cn: 英语 actuate 最初用于机器与弹簧。

items.en: Technical use survives in actuators; the 'motivate' sense is now formal.
items.cn: 技术用法保留在 actuator 一词中；「驱使」义如今偏正式。

note.en: The first group gathers the agere family and its offspring; the second gathers verbs of setting things or people in motion.
note.cn: 第一组收 agere 词族及其派生词；第二组收让物或人动起来的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of triggering a device.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「启动、触发」。

entries.definition: The device that carries out the triggering, common in engineering.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「执行器」，工程常用。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning 'real'; spelling near, meaning far.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「实际的」；拼写相近，意义不同。

entries.definition: To set off a device or a chain of events.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「触发、引发」。

entries.definition: To make a system or plan start working.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「激活、使生效」。

entries.definition: To drive a person forward by force or motive.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「驱使、推动（人）」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the drive-root act- and the engineering word actuator; the abstract hooks picture a lever thrown.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「驱动」词根 act- 与工程词 actuator；抽象记忆点想象扳动连杆。

normal.en: Actuate is act- plus -ate: to put into act.
normal.cn: actuate 是 act- 加 -ate：使之进入行动。

normal.en: An actuator is the part that actuates a machine.
normal.cn: actuator 是执行 actuate 的部件。

normal.en: Be actuated by is the formal pattern for motives.
normal.cn: be actuated by 是表示动机的正式结构。

normal.en: Activate is the everyday word; actuate is technical.
normal.cn: activate 是日常用词，actuate 偏技术。

normal.en: The noun is actuation.
normal.cn: 名词是 actuation。

abstract.en: Picture a hand throwing a big brass lever.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手扳下黄铜大连杆。

abstract.en: Picture gears waking up one by one.
abstract.cn: 想象齿轮被一个个唤醒。

abstract.en: Picture conscience pressing the start button of a decision.
abstract.cn: 想象良知按下决定的启动键。

examples.en: A lever actuates the safety brake when the cable snaps.
examples.cn: 缆绳断裂时连杆会触发安全制动。

examples.en: The relay actuates the alarm circuit within milliseconds.
examples.cn: 继电器在几毫秒内接通报警电路。

examples.en: He was actuated by a desire to defend his colleagues.
examples.cn: 驱使他的是保护同事的愿望。

branches.en: The mechanical start of a device.
branches.cn: 装置的机械性启动。

branches.en: Machine and mind share the same switch.
branches.cn: 机器与心智共用同一个开关。

branches.en: Engineering keeps this sense alive in actuator.
branches.cn: 工程学在 actuator 中保留了这个义项。

definition_zh: 敏锐；精明；洞察力；（某一领域的）才干
definition_en: the ability to think quickly and make sharp judgments, especially in a practical field
core_image: 谈判桌上，一眼看穿对方报价里的漏洞
scene: 拍卖会里，别人还在犹豫，他已经从落款和纸张判断出这幅画的年代。Her business acumen turned a small shop into a chain.
sceneCN: 这里 acumen 是「精明、商业头脑」（第 1 个义项：在实务中做出敏锐判断的能力）；句意为她的商业头脑把小店做成了连锁。

derivatives.zh: 同根形容词，义为「敏锐的；剧烈的」
同根名词，义为「敏锐度」
同根副词，义为「敏锐地；强烈地」

senses.title: Sharp judgment
senses.definition: the ability to see quickly what is true or useful
senses.definitionCN: 迅速看出真实或有用之处的能力
senses.example: Her business acumen turned a small shop into a chain.
senses.exampleCN: 她的商业头脑把小店做成了连锁。
senses.why: Latin acumen meant 'a sharp point', so the mind is pictured as a blade that cuts through confusion.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 acumen 意为「尖点」，因此心智被想象成切开混乱的刀刃。

senses.title: Practical skill in a field
senses.definition: specialized shrewdness in business, law, or another practical area
senses.definitionCN: 在商业、法律等实务领域的专门精明
senses.example: The firm hired him for his legal acumen.
senses.exampleCN: 公司因他的法律才干而聘用他。
senses.why: The word is often paired with a field name, because sharpness shows itself in a particular trade.
senses.whyCN: 这个词常与领域名称搭配，因为敏锐总是在具体行当里显现。

senses.title: Keen perception of detail
senses.definition: a quick, exact awareness of small differences or hidden faults
senses.definitionCN: 对细微差别或隐藏缺陷的快速精确察觉
senses.example: With rare acumen she spotted the forged signature at once.
senses.exampleCN: 她以罕见的洞察力一眼识破了伪造的签名。
senses.why: A sharp point finds the smallest crack; keen perception is the same point applied to detail.
senses.whyCN: 尖点能找到最细的裂缝；对细节的敏锐感知就是把这份「尖」用在细处。

intro.cn: acumen 直接来自拉丁语 acumen（尖点），源自 acuere（磨尖），是 acute 的词根。

entries.definition: Practical cleverness in dealing with people.

abstract.en: Picture a blade cutting clean through fog.

derivatives.zh: 由本词加副词后缀构成，义为「坚决地」

senses.title: Unshakable in opinion
senses.definition: refusing to change one's mind no matter the persuasion
senses.definitionCN: 无论怎么劝说都不改变主意
senses.example: The boy remained adamant about not giving up his seat.
senses.exampleCN: 男孩坚决不让出座位。
senses.why: Adamant once named the hardest imagined stone; a mind like that stone cannot be dented.
senses.whyCN: adamant 曾指想象中最硬的石头；如那石头般的心无法被压出凹痕。

senses.title: Old use: a substance of extreme hardness
senses.definition: in older texts, a legendary stone hard as diamond, later applied to diamond itself
senses.definitionCN: 旧文本中指传说中硬度如金刚石的石头，后来也指金刚石本身
senses.example: Old travellers swore the tower's gates were barred with adamant.
senses.exampleCN: 老旅人坚称那座塔门用坚不可摧之物封死。
senses.why: The noun is the older sense: the hard stone came first, and the stubborn mind borrowed its hardness.
senses.whyCN: 名词义更古老：坚硬的石头先出现，「坚决的心智」借用了它的硬度。

intro.en: Adamant comes through Latin and Greek to a word for the hardest stone, later applied to diamond.
intro.cn: adamant 经拉丁语与希腊语传来，指最坚硬的石头，后来也指金刚石。

items.en: The reconstructed root *dem- is thought to mean 'to force, to tame'.
items.cn: 一般认为重构词根 *dem- 意为「强制、驯服」。

items.en: Greek adamas meant 'unbreakable, hardest steel or stone', a- with a negative sense.
items.cn: 希腊语 adamas 意为「不可破碎的、最硬的钢或石」，a- 带否定意味。

items.en: Latin adamantem kept the meaning of the hardest substance.
items.cn: 拉丁语 adamantem 保留「最坚硬之物」的意思。

items.en: Old French adamaunt brought it to English as the name of the hardest stone.
items.cn: 古法语 adamaunt 把它带入英语，指最硬的石头。

items.en: The adjective sense of 'unyielding mind' is now dominant; diamond took over the stone sense.
items.cn: 「不肯让步的心智」这一形容词义如今占主流；石头义由 diamond 接管。

note.en: The first group gathers the hard-stone family; the second gathers words for unshakable positions.
note.cn: 第一组收「硬石」词族；第二组收表示立场坚定的词。

entries.definition: A literary adjective for hard as diamond.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「坚硬如金刚石的」，多见于文学。

entries.definition: A cousin spelling of the same Greek word, now the gemstone name.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「金刚石」，与 adamant 同出希腊语一名。

entries.definition: A chemistry name for a cage-shaped hydrocarbon, named for its stability.
entries.definitionCN: 化学名词，义为「金刚烷」，因结构稳固得名。

entries.definition: Firm and not giving way.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「强硬的、不让步的」。

entries.definition: Unable or unwilling to bend.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不灵活的、顽固的」。

entries.definition: Impossible to appease or soften.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「难以平息的」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the Greek hard-stone word and the diamond cousin; the abstract hooks picture a wall that will not move.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用希腊语「硬石」词与同源的 diamond；抽象记忆点想象一堵纹丝不动的墙。

normal.en: Adamant and diamond come from the same Greek word.
normal.cn: adamant 与 diamond 出自同一个希腊语词。

normal.en: Adamant about is the standard preposition pattern.
normal.cn: adamant about 是标准介词搭配。

normal.en: The a- in Greek adamas works like 'un-'.
normal.cn: 希腊语 adamas 中的 a- 相当于「不」。

normal.en: Adamantly is the adverb for firm refusal.
normal.cn: adamantly 是表示坚决拒绝的副词。

normal.en: Adamant is stronger than firm or stubborn in tone.
normal.cn: 在语气上 adamant 比 firm 或 stubborn 更强。

abstract.en: Picture a stone wall facing a storm without moving an inch.
abstract.cn: 想象一堵石墙在风暴中寸步不移。

abstract.en: Picture a diamond that no hammer can scratch.
abstract.cn: 想象锤子也划不动的金刚石。

abstract.en: Picture a child shaking his head three times in a row.
abstract.cn: 想象孩子连摇三次头。

examples.en: The boy remained adamant about not giving up his seat.
examples.cn: 男孩坚决不让出座位。

examples.en: She was adamant that the report be published unchanged.
examples.cn: 她坚决要求报告原样发表。

examples.en: Despite the warnings, the committee stayed adamant.
examples.cn: 尽管有警告，委员会依旧不让步。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿达门特」——阿哥把门顶得死死的，谁劝都不开，就是坚决。

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the unshakable mind back to the legendary hard stone from which the image grew.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从不可动摇的心智，回溯到意象来源——传说中的硬石。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a stone that nothing can dent
core.cn: 核心意象：怎么敲都无痕的石头

branches.en: A mind that no persuasion dents.
branches.cn: 任何劝说都压不出痕的心智。

branches.en: The legendary stone behind the image.
branches.cn: 意象背后的传说硬石。

branches.en: The mind borrows the stone's hardness.
branches.cn: 心智借用了石头的硬度。

branches.en: Common with about and that in modern speech.
branches.cn: 现代口语常与 about 和 that 搭配。

branches.en: Both senses say the same thing: it will not change.
branches.cn: 两个义项说的是同一件事：不会改变。

intro.en: The word is a Greek negative a- on a root about forcing and breaking, and the family keeps diamond and adamantine.
intro.cn: 这个词是希腊语否定前缀 a- 加上与「强制、破碎」相关的词根，词族保留 diamond 与 adamantine。

latinIntro.en: Latin adamantem carried the Greek word into European languages.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 adamantem 把希腊语词带入欧洲各语言。

definition_zh: 添加；增加；加上；补充说；相加
definition_en: to put something together with something else, or to join numbers or words, so that the amount, total or effect becomes greater
core_image: 往已经盛着水的杯子里再倒一勺糖：东西叠上去，分量就变了
scene: 火锅端上桌时汤底还不够辣，朋友拿起辣椒罐又抖了两下。He added more chilli to the soup.
sceneCN: 这里 add 是「添加、放入」（第 1 个义项：把某物放进已有的东西里）；句意为他又往汤里加了辣椒。

pos.zh: 动词：添加；增加；加上；补充说；相加
及物动词：把……加入；把（数字）相加

senses.title: To put an ingredient or object into something
senses.definition: to put a substance, ingredient or object into a container or mixture that already has something in it
senses.definitionCN: 把某种物质、配料或物件放进已有东西的容器或混合物中
senses.example: Add a pinch of salt to the boiling water.
senses.exampleCN: 往滚水里加一小撮盐。
senses.why: Latin addere is ad- 'to' plus dare 'give': the core action is giving one thing to another, so that two things stand together.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 addere 由 ad-「向」与 dare「给」构成：核心动作是把一个东西给到另一个东西上，让两者并置。

senses.title: To join numbers to get a total
senses.definition: to put two or more numbers or amounts together in order to work out their total
senses.definitionCN: 把两个或更多的数或量合在一起，求出它们的总数
senses.example: If you add seven and three, you get ten.
senses.exampleCN: 七加三等于十。
senses.why: Numbers are treated like objects in a pile: each is given to the pile, and the pile is then counted.
senses.whyCN: 数字被当作堆在一起的物件：每个都「给」到堆上，再数这一堆的总量。

senses.title: To say something more
senses.definition: to say something further, especially to give extra information or to make a remark after what has already been said
senses.definitionCN: 再说一些话，尤指在已说的话之后补充信息或加一句评论
senses.example: She added that the meeting would start an hour later.
senses.exampleCN: 她补充说会议将推迟一小时开始。
senses.why: Words are given to the conversation the same way sugar is given to tea: the sentence is placed on top of what was already there.
senses.whyCN: 话语被「给」到对话里，就像糖被给到茶里：新句子叠在已经说过的话之上。

senses.title: To give an extra quality
senses.definition: to bring a quality such as flavour, colour or atmosphere to something, so that it becomes richer
senses.definitionCN: 为某物带来味道、色彩或气氛等特质，使之更丰富
senses.example: A few candles added warmth to the plain room.
senses.exampleCN: 几支蜡烛给这间素净的屋子增添了暖意。
senses.why: What is given here is not a thing but a quality; the gesture of giving is unchanged, only the gift is abstract.
senses.whyCN: 这里给出去的不是物件而是一种特质；「给」的动作没有变，变的只是所给之物的抽象程度。

senses.title: To include someone in an online contact list
senses.definition: to include someone in your list of friends or contacts on a social media or messaging service
senses.definitionCN: 把某人加入社交平台或通讯软件的好友、联系人列表
senses.example: He added me on the app the day after the party.
senses.exampleCN: 聚会第二天他在那个应用上把我加为好友。
senses.why: The list is a container like the cup, and a person is the thing given to it; the old gesture simply moved online.
senses.whyCN: 好友列表就像那只杯子，人就是被放进去的东西；古老的「给」只是搬到了网上。

senses.title: To make a problem or feeling greater
senses.titleCN: 使增加；加重（麻烦、花费、情绪）
senses.definition: to increase the size, cost or unpleasantness of something that is already there, usually unintentionally
senses.definitionCN: 使已经存在的事物规模、花费或糟糕程度上升，通常是并非有意造成的
senses.example: The long delay added to everyone's frustration.
senses.exampleCN: 漫长的延误让大家更加烦躁。
senses.why: Nothing new is created; one load is laid on another, and the whole pile grows heavier.
senses.whyCN: 并没有造出新东西，只是把一份负担叠到另一份上，整堆就更沉了。

senses.title: Add up: to calculate a total
senses.definition: in the phrase add up, to calculate the total of several numbers or amounts
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 add up，把若干数字或金额加起来求出总数
senses.example: Please add up these receipts before we leave.
senses.exampleCN: 我们走之前请把这些收据加起来。
senses.why: The base sense of putting things to one heap is applied to figures: the heap is then counted as a single amount.
senses.whyCN: 把东西堆到一起的基本义被用到数字上：堆好之后再当作一个总量来数。

senses.title: Add up: to seem reasonable
senses.definition: in the phrase add up, of facts or accounts, to seem reasonable and consistent when they are considered together
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 add up，指各种事实或说法放在一起看时显得合理、前后一致
senses.example: His story sounds fine, but the dates just don't add up.
senses.exampleCN: 他的说法听着不错，可日期就是对不上。
senses.why: If the parts do not sum correctly, the account is wrong; the arithmetic image is used for a story that fails to hang together.
senses.whyCN: 如果各部分加起来对不上总数，这笔账就有问题；于是用算术的画面来形容一个前后拼不拢的说法。

intro.en: Add is Latin addere taken into English almost unchanged; the whole family grows from the verb dare, 'to give'.
intro.cn: add 几乎原样借自拉丁语 addere，整个词族都从动词 dare「给」生长出来。

items.en: Dare meant 'to give' and is one of the oldest recorded Latin verbs. It goes back to a reconstructed Indo-European root usually written *deh₃-, 'to give'.
items.cn: dare 意为「给」，是拉丁语中有记录的最古老动词之一。它可追溯到一般写作 *deh₃- 的原始印欧语重构词根，意为「给」。

items.en: The prefix ad- 'to' plus dare formed addere, 'to give to, put to, add'. Classical Latin already used it for both objects and numbers.
items.cn: 前缀 ad- 表示「向」，与 dare 合成 addere，意为「给到……上、放上去、增加」。古典拉丁语已用它表示物件与数字。

items.en: English took add straight from Latin, and it is recorded from the late fourteenth century in the general sense of putting one thing to another.
items.cn: 英语直接从拉丁语借入 add，自十四世纪后期有记录，泛指把一物加到另一物上。

items.en: The arithmetic sense settled early, and the phrase add up, first meaning to sum figures, appears in the eighteenth century.
items.cn: 算术义很早就固定下来；短语 add up 最初表示把数字加总，见于十八世纪。

items.en: New containers brought new uses: add a friend, add to cart, add a comment. The old pattern of giving one thing to another is unchanged.
items.cn: 新的「容器」带来新用法：加好友、加入购物车、添加评论；「把一物给到另一物上」的旧结构没有变。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the derived nouns and one snaky false friend; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of putting something in or joining it on.
note.cn: 形近组收本词的派生名词，外加一个只是长得像的词；近义组收放入、附加、插入与求和一类的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for the act of adding, the thing added, or the arithmetic operation of finding a sum.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「添加、增加物、加法」，指添加的行为、被添加之物或求和的运算。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning extra or added on top of what already exists.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「额外的、附加的」，指在已有之物上再加的。

entries.definition: Something added at the end of a book or agreement, from the Latin gerundive of addere.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「补遗、附加条款」，指书或协议末尾追加的内容，来自拉丁语 addere 的动形词。

entries.definition: A small poisonous snake; it looks like add plus -er but descends from Old English nædre.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「蝰蛇」；只是拼写相近，词源不同，它来自古英语 nædre，与 add 无关。

entries.definition: To have something as a part of a group or whole, rather than putting it in from outside.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「包括、包含」，指某物本来就是整体的一部分，而不是从外面放进去。

entries.definition: To attach something at the end of a document or list; formal and often technical.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「附加、附上」，指在文件或列表末尾添上，语气正式，多用于技术语境。

entries.definition: To put something inside something else, often into a text or a narrow space.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「插入、嵌入」，指把某物放进另一物内部，常用于文本或狭窄空间。

entries.definition: As a verb, to add amounts or figures together, or to summarize; the mathematical twin of add.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「合计、总结」，指把金额或数字加在一起，是 add 在算术上的近义词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the Latin verb dare and the everyday patterns add appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些钩子借助拉丁动词 dare 与 add 常见的日常结构。

normal.en: Addere is ad- plus dare, so to add is literally to give something to something.
normal.cn: addere 就是 ad- 加 dare，所以「添加」字面上就是「把一个东西给另一个」。

normal.en: Addition, additional and additionally all keep the same base.
normal.cn: addition、additional、additionally 都保留同一个词基。

normal.en: You add milk to tea, add numbers in maths, and add a word at the end of a sentence.
normal.cn: 往茶里加牛奶，在算术里加数字，在句子末尾加一句话，用的都是同一个词。

normal.en: Add up means both to total figures and, informally, to make sense.
normal.cn: add up 既指把数字加总，也口语地指「说得通」。

normal.en: Add fuel to the fire and add insult to injury both mean making a bad thing worse.
normal.cn: add fuel to the fire 与 add insult to injury 都是把坏事弄得更糟。

abstract.en: A cup already full can still take one more spoon of sugar; there is always room for one more.
abstract.cn: 杯子已经满了，却还能再放一勺糖：总还有放一样东西的余地。

abstract.en: Growing a pile and growing a number are the same gesture in two worlds.
abstract.cn: 堆高东西和累加数字，是同一个动作在两个世界里发生。

abstract.en: A story adds up only when every piece has been given its place.
abstract.cn: 一个说法要每一块都放对位置，才「加得起来」。

examples.en: Add a little milk if the sauce looks too thick.
examples.cn: 酱汁看着太稠就再加一点牛奶。

examples.en: She added my number to the group chat.
examples.cn: 她把我的号码加进了群聊。

examples.en: The numbers don't add up, so check the bill again.
examples.cn: 这些数对不上，再核对一遍账单吧。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿德」——阿德往锅里又加一勺，味道就对了：添加、加上。

root: 拉丁语 addere 由 ad-「向」+ dare「给」构成，字面是「给到……上」，故有「添加、加上」。dare 可追溯到原始印欧语重构词根 *deh₃-「给」；addition、additional 均由这个词干加后缀构成。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses perform one act of giving something to something already there: an ingredient, a number, a remark, a quality, a contact, a burden, a column of figures, or a set of facts.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项做的都是同一个动作——把某样东西给到已有之物上：配料、数字、一句话、一种特质、一个联系人、一份负担、一列数字，或一组事实。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one spoon of sugar is tipped into a cup that already holds water.
core.cn: 核心意象：一勺糖被倒进已经盛着水的杯子里。

branches.en: THE CONTAINER: a cup, a recipe or a contact list receives one more thing.
branches.cn: 容器线：杯子、菜谱或联系人列表再接收一样东西。

branches.en: THE NUMBERS: figures are heaped and then counted as one sum.
branches.cn: 数字线：把数堆在一起，再当作一个总和来数。

branches.en: THE REMARK: one more sentence is laid on top of what has been said.
branches.cn: 言语线：在已经说过的话上再叠一句。

branches.en: THE QUALITY: what is given is warmth, colour or flavour rather than an object.
branches.cn: 特质线：给出去的是暖意、色彩或味道，而不是物件。

branches.en: THE FIGURE: a heavier pile and a story that will not sum both show the arithmetic image at work.
branches.cn: 比喻线：更沉的负担与加不拢的说法，都显出算术这一比喻在起作用。

intro.en: Add is a Latin prefix plus the verb dare, and English adds its usual noun and adjective suffixes to the stem.
intro.cn: add 由一个拉丁前缀与动词 dare 构成，英语再给这个词干加上常见的名词与形容词后缀。

latinIntro.en: Dare, addere, additio and addendum are all recorded Latin forms; the Indo-European root behind dare is a reconstruction.
latinIntro.cn: dare、addere、additio 与 addendum 都是有记录的拉丁语形式；dare 背后的印欧词根属于重构形式。

items.exampleCN: 这个前缀把「给」这个动作指向一个目标。

items.example: It is one of the oldest Latin verbs.
items.exampleCN: 它是拉丁语中最古老的动词之一。

items.example: It forms addendum in Latin and English.

items.meaning: to put one thing to another
items.example: The English verb kept the Latin shape.
items.exampleCN: 这个英语动词几乎保留了拉丁语的原形。

definition_zh: 附录；补遗；补充条款
definition_en: an extra item, note, or section added to a book, document, or agreement
core_image: 合同签完又多钉进去一页补充
scene: 合同双方都签了字，律师忽然想起漏了一条免责条款，当场多拟了一页订在后面。The lawyer drafted an addendum to cover the missing clause.
sceneCN: 这里 addendum 是「附录、补充条款」（第 1 个义项：加在文件后面补充内容的部分）；句意为律师草拟了一份附录补上遗漏的条款。

derivatives.zh: 同根基础词，义为「添加」
同根名词，义为「加法；增加物」

senses.title: A section added to a document
senses.definition: a part added after a document is finished, to supply something missing or new
senses.definitionCN: 文件完成后追加的部分，用以补充遗漏或新增内容
senses.example: The lawyer drafted an addendum to cover the missing clause.
senses.exampleCN: 律师草拟了一份附录补上遗漏的条款。
senses.why: Latin dare means 'to give'; an addendum is what is given to the text after the text is done.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 dare 意为「给予」；addendum 就是文本完成后被「补给」文本的东西。

senses.title: A late addition to a book
senses.definition: a note or correction appended to a published book
senses.definitionCN: 附在已出版书籍末尾的说明或更正
senses.example: The second printing carries an addendum correcting two dates.
senses.exampleCN: 第二次印刷附了一份更正两个年份的补遗。
senses.why: What was discovered too late to enter the main text is given its own little tail page.
senses.whyCN: 来不及进入正文的发现，被「补给」了自己的一页小尾巴。

intro.en: Addendum is the Latin gerundive of addere, 'to be added', from ad- 'to' plus dare 'to give'.
intro.cn: addendum 是拉丁语 addere（增添）的动形词，意为「应被加上之物」，由 ad-（向）加 dare（给予）构成。

items.en: The reconstructed root *do- meant 'to give'.
items.cn: 重构词根 *do- 意为「给予」。

items.en: dare meant 'to give'; addere meant 'to give to, to add'.
items.cn: dare 意为「给予」；addere 意为「加给、增添」。

items.en: addendum was the gerundive: 'the thing that must be added'.
items.cn: addendum 是动形词：「必须被加上之物」。

items.en: English borrowed the word for appended matter in books.
items.cn: 英语借入该词，指书末附加的内容。

items.en: Now common in contracts as well as books; plural addenda survives in formal use.
items.cn: 如今合同与书籍都用；正式场合保留拉丁式复数 addenda。

note.en: The first group gathers the dare family of adding words; the second gathers words for appended material.
note.cn: 第一组收 dare 词族的「添加」词；第二组收表示附加内容的词。

entries.definition: The Latin-style plural of addendum.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，addendum 的拉丁式复数。

entries.definition: The act or result of adding; a longer-lived cousin.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「加法；增加物」，同根近亲。

entries.definition: To cite as evidence; only the first letters overlap, root differs.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「引证」；仅开头拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: A body of extra material at the end of a book.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「附录」，常指书末整块附加材料。

entries.definition: A section or building added to something larger.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「附件；附属建筑」。

entries.definition: Something added to complete or extend a work.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「补充；增刊」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the dare root and the contract scene; the abstract hooks picture an extra page pinned at the end.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用 dare 词根与合同场景；抽象记忆点想象末尾多钉一页。

normal.en: Addendum is 'the thing to be added': ad- plus dare.
normal.cn: addendum 意为「应加之物」：ad- 加 dare。

normal.en: The formal plural is addenda.
normal.cn: 正式复数是 addenda。

normal.en: Contract addendum is common in legal English.
normal.cn: contract addendum 在法律英语中常见。

normal.en: An addendum comes after the main text is done.
normal.cn: addendum 出现在正文完成之后。

normal.en: It shares the root with add and addition.
normal.cn: 它与 add 和 addition 同根。

abstract.en: Picture a page slipped in and stapled after signatures.
abstract.cn: 想象签字后又订进去的一页纸。

abstract.en: Picture a book growing a small extra tail.
abstract.cn: 想象书长出一条小尾巴。

abstract.en: Picture a hand adding one last brick to a finished wall.
abstract.cn: 想象往完工的墙上补最后一块砖。

examples.en: The lawyer drafted an addendum to cover the missing clause.
examples.cn: 律师草拟了一份附录补上遗漏的条款。

examples.en: Please review the addenda before signing the agreement.
examples.cn: 签署协议前请先审阅各份补充条款。

examples.en: The second printing carries an addendum correcting two dates.
examples.cn: 第二次印刷附了一份更正两个年份的补遗。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额顶达姆」——合同额头上多顶出一页补丁，就是附录。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ dare（给予）→ addere（增添）→ addendum（应加之物）；核心义是「事后补送给文本的东西」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from appended contract matter, to late corrections in a book.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从合同的追加条款，走到书籍的迟来补正。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an extra page pinned after the last page
core.cn: 核心意象：末页之后多钉的一页

branches.en: The extra clause that completes a contract.
branches.cn: 补全合同的追加条款。

branches.en: The late note that mends a published book.
branches.cn: 修补已出版书籍的迟来说明。

branches.en: Both senses arrive after the work is finished.
branches.cn: 两个义项都出现在工作完成之后。

branches.en: Legal English keeps this sense busy.
branches.cn: 法律英语频繁使用这个义项。

branches.en: Both rest on the Latin idea of 'giving to'.
branches.cn: 两者都立足拉丁语「加给」的观念。

intro.en: The word joins the prefix ad- with the give-root dend-, and the family spreads through add, addition, and date-related words.
intro.cn: 这个词把前缀 ad- 与「给」词根 dend- 结合，词族遍布 add、addition 及与日期相关的词。

latinIntro.en: Latin addere and its gerundive addendum are the recorded sources.
latinIntro.cn: 记录在案的来源是拉丁语 addere 及其动形词 addendum。

latinEntries.meaning: the thing that must be added

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「加法；增加物」
形容词，义为「额外的」

definition_zh: 使混乱；使昏乱；（蛋）变质；变糊涂
definition_en: to confuse someone's mind, or to go bad and rotten, as an egg does
core_image: 一枚放坏的蛋，摇起来浑浊一片
scene: 连考三门之后，他的脑子里只剩嗡嗡声，公式全搅成一团。Too many formulas addled the student's brain.
sceneCN: 这里 addle 是「使混乱、使昏乱」（第 1 个义项：搅乱头脑）；句意为公式太多把学生的脑子搅浑了。

derivatives.zh: 由本词过去分词转形容词，义为「混乱的；糊涂的；（蛋）变质的」
由本词构成的复合形容词，义为「头脑混乱的」

senses.title: To confuse the mind
senses.definition: to make someone unable to think clearly
senses.definitionCN: 使某人无法清晰思考
senses.example: Too many formulas addled the student's brain.
senses.exampleCN: 公式太多把学生的脑子搅浑了。
senses.why: A rotten egg turns cloudy and useless; an addled mind is the same mixture where thought no longer separates.
senses.whyCN: 坏蛋变得浑浊无用；昏乱的头脑正是同样的混浊，思想再也无法分层。

senses.title: To go rotten, as an egg
senses.definition: of an egg, to spoil so that the contents turn mixed and cloudy
senses.definitionCN: 指鸡蛋变坏，内容物浑浊混合
senses.example: The eggs addled in the summer heat.
senses.exampleCN: 鸡蛋在暑热中放坏了。
senses.why: This is the original sense: the egg's clear parts collapse into one turbid mass.
senses.whyCN: 这是本源义：蛋里清澈的部分塌缩成一团浑浊。

intro.en: Addle comes from Old English adela, 'liquid filth, puddle', first used of eggs gone bad.
intro.cn: addle 源自古英语 adela（污水、浊液），最初用于变质的蛋。

items.en: adela meant 'filthy liquid or puddle'.
items.cn: adela 意为「污水、浊洼」。

items.en: Cousin forms in Germanic languages also name muddy liquid; the deeper root is uncertain.
items.cn: 日耳曼诸语言的同族词也指浑浊液体；更深的词根来源不确定。

items.en: addle described eggs whose contents had gone cloudy and spoiled.
items.cn: addle 描述内容物浑浊变坏的蛋。

items.en: The 'confused mind' sense grew from the rotten-egg picture.
items.cn: 「头脑混乱」义由坏蛋意象长出。

items.en: The adjective addled is now the commonest form, mostly of brains and thoughts.
items.cn: 形容词 addled 如今最常见，多用于头脑与思绪。

note.en: The first group gathers look-alike words of different roots; the second gathers words for confusion and spoilage.
note.cn: 第一组收词源不同但形近的词；第二组收表示混乱与变质的词。

entries.definition: A humorous old adjective for hopelessly confused.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「头昏脑胀的」，多见于旧式幽默文字。

entries.definition: An old nickname for a muddled person.
entries.definitionCN: 旧式称呼，义为「糊脑袋的人」。

entries.definition: A small venomous snake; only spelling near, root unrelated.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「蝰蛇」；仅拼写相近，词源无关。

entries.definition: To mix things up into confusion.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「搅乱、弄混」。

entries.definition: To make someone dazed and unable to think.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「使昏乱、使迷糊」。

entries.definition: To decay and go bad.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「腐烂、变坏」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the rotten-egg origin and the addled-brain collocation; the abstract hooks picture murky water.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用坏蛋的来源与 addled-brain 搭配；抽象记忆点想象浑浊的水。

normal.en: Addle began as bad egg liquid: adela, muddy water.
normal.cn: addle 起于坏蛋的浊液：adela，污水。

normal.en: Addle one's brain is the classic phrase.
normal.cn: addle one's brain 是经典搭配。

normal.en: The adjective addled describes both eggs and minds.
normal.cn: 形容词 addled 既形容蛋也形容头脑。

normal.en: Muddle rhymes with addle and means confusion too.
normal.cn: muddle 与 addle 押韵，同样表示混乱。

normal.en: It is informal and slightly humorous in modern use.
normal.cn: 现代用法偏非正式，略带幽默。

abstract.en: Picture an egg shaken into cloudy soup.
abstract.cn: 想象鸡蛋被摇成一碗浑汤。

abstract.en: Picture a pond stirred until nothing can be seen.
abstract.cn: 想象池塘被搅到什么都看不清。

abstract.en: Picture formulas swirling into grey fog in a head.
abstract.cn: 想象公式在头脑里旋成灰色迷雾。

examples.en: Too many formulas addled the student's brain.
examples.cn: 公式太多把学生的脑子搅浑了。

examples.en: The eggs addled in the summer heat.
examples.cn: 鸡蛋在暑热中放坏了。

examples.en: Late nights left him addled for the whole morning.
examples.cn: 熬夜让他整个上午昏昏沉沉。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「阿豆」——豆浆搅浑了脑子也浑了，就是搅乱。

root: 古英语 adela（污水、浊液）；核心义是「清水变浑汤——蛋如此，头脑也如此」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from spoiling eggs to confusing minds, both by the same picture of turning clear into muddy.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从蛋的变质走到头脑的昏乱，共用同一幅「清变浑」的图景。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: clear water stirred into cloudy mud
core.cn: 核心意象：清水被搅成浑泥汤

branches.en: The mind stirred till thought will not settle.
branches.cn: 头脑被搅到思绪无法沉淀。

branches.en: The egg whose parts collapse into turbid mass.
branches.cn: 内容物塌成浑浊一团的蛋。

branches.en: Both senses are the same muddying, of egg or of mind.
branches.cn: 两个义项是同一场「变浑」，发生在蛋里或脑子里。

branches.en: This is the older, original sense.
branches.cn: 这是更古老的本源义。

branches.en: Modern usage keeps this sense alive mainly in addled.
branches.cn: 现代用法主要通过 addled 保留这个义项。

intro.en: Addle is a plain Germanic stem with no Latin prefix; the family is small and mostly English-made compounds.
intro.cn: addle 是单纯的日耳曼词干，没有拉丁前缀；词族很小，多为英语自造复合词。

latinIntro.en: No Latin kinship is recorded; the deeper Germanic root is uncertain.
latinIntro.cn: 无拉丁亲缘记录；更深的日耳曼词根来源不确定。

derivatives.zh: 形容词，义为「混乱的；（蛋）变质的」
复合形容词，义为「头脑混乱的」

definition_zh: 引证；举出（证据、理由）
definition_en: to offer facts or reasons as evidence in support of an argument
core_image: 把一摞证据一页页摆到辩论桌上
scene: 听证会上，律师翻开文件夹，把三份原始记录摆上桌。The counsel adduced fresh documents to prove the timeline.
sceneCN: 这里 adduce 是「引证、举出」（第 1 个义项：提出证据或理由支持论点）；句意为律师出示新文件证明时间线。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「引证；举出证据」（另在解剖学中指内收）
同根词，义为「推断」，反方向使用同一词根

senses.title: To offer evidence for an argument
senses.definition: to put forward facts, documents, or examples as proof
senses.definitionCN: 提出事实、文件或例证作为证明
senses.example: The counsel adduced fresh documents to prove the timeline.
senses.exampleCN: 律师出示新文件证明时间线。
senses.why: Latin ducere means 'to lead'; to adduce is to lead evidence forward, out of the file and onto the table.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ducere 意为「引导」；adduce 就是把证据从卷宗里领出来，引到桌面上。

senses.title: To cite reasons or examples
senses.definition: to mention reasons or instances in support of a claim
senses.definitionCN: 提及理由或实例以支持某个主张
senses.example: He adduced several precedents from earlier disputes.
senses.exampleCN: 他援引了早先争端中的几个先例。
senses.why: Reasons, like documents, are led out into the open where the audience can inspect them.
senses.whyCN: 理由如同文件，也要被领到明处，供听者查验。

intro.en: Adduce joins Latin ad- 'to' with ducere 'to lead', meaning 'to lead forward (as evidence)'.
intro.cn: adduce 由拉丁语 ad-（向）加 ducere（引导）构成，意为「把（证据）引上前」。

items.en: The reconstructed root *deuk- meant 'to lead, to pull'.
items.cn: 重构词根 *deuk- 意为「引导、牵拉」。

items.en: ducere meant 'to lead', the root of duke and duct.
items.cn: ducere 意为「引导」，是 duke 与 duct 的词根。

items.en: adducere meant 'to lead to, to bring forward'.
items.cn: adducere 意为「引到、带来」。

items.en: English adduce settled into legal and scholarly argument.
items.cn: 英语 adduce 定着于法律与学术论证。

items.en: Now formal; everyday speech prefers cite or present.
items.cn: 如今属正式用语；日常口语多用 cite 或 present。

note.en: The first group gathers the ducere family; the second gathers verbs of putting forward proof.
note.cn: 第一组收 ducere 词族；第二组收提出证明的动词。

entries.definition: To work a conclusion out, leading thought downward from facts.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「推断」，同一词根的反向使用。

entries.definition: To lead someone or something into a state.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「诱导、引起」。

entries.definition: An appendix; only the opening letters overlap, root differs.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「附录」；仅开头拼写相近，词源不同。

entries.definition: To mention a source or example as support.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「引用、引证」。

entries.definition: To lay something before a court or audience.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「提交、出示」。

entries.definition: To back a claim with solid evidence.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「证实、为主张提供依据」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the ducere root and the courtroom scene; the abstract hooks picture documents led onto a table.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用 ducere 词根与法庭场景；抽象记忆点想象文件被引上桌。

normal.en: Adduce is ad- plus ducere: to lead evidence forward.
normal.cn: adduce 是 ad- 加 ducere：把证据引上前。

normal.en: Adduce evidence is the core collocation.
normal.cn: adduce evidence 是核心搭配。

normal.en: Deduce runs the same root in reverse: lead down to a conclusion.
normal.cn: deduce 把同一词根反过来用：引出结论。

normal.en: The word is formal, at home in law and scholarship.
normal.cn: 这个词很正式，常用于法律与学术。

normal.en: Everyday speech says cite instead.
normal.cn: 日常口语改用 cite。

abstract.en: Picture a lawyer sliding a folder across the bench.
abstract.cn: 想象律师把文件夹推过法官席。

abstract.en: Picture a chain of evidence pulled forward link by link.
abstract.cn: 想象证据链被一环环牵引向前。

abstract.en: Picture a teacher leading examples up onto the blackboard.
abstract.cn: 想象老师把例证引上黑板。

examples.en: The counsel adduced fresh documents to prove the timeline.
examples.cn: 律师出示新文件证明时间线。

examples.en: She adduced market data to support her forecast.
examples.cn: 她引用市场数据支持自己的预测。

examples.en: He adduced several precedents from earlier disputes.
examples.cn: 他援引了早先争端中的几个先例。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额丢斯」——把证据往桌上一丢就齐了，就是引证。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ ducere（引导）→ adducere（引上前）；核心义是「把证据或理由领到论辩的桌面上」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from offering documents as proof, to citing reasons and precedents.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从出示文件作证，走到援引理由与先例。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: evidence led forward onto the table
core.cn: 核心意象：证据被引上桌面

branches.en: Documents and facts led out as proof.
branches.cn: 被领出作证的事实与文件。

branches.en: Reasons and precedents led out in argument.
branches.cn: 论证中被援引的理由与先例。

branches.en: Both senses lead something out for inspection.
branches.cn: 两个义项都是把某物领出来供查验。

branches.en: Legal argument is the natural home of this sense.
branches.cn: 法律论证是这个义项的自然阵地。

branches.en: Both stand on ducere, the Latin verb of leading.
branches.cn: 两者都立足拉丁语「引导」动词 ducere。

intro.en: The verb joins the prefix ad- with the lead-root duc-, and the ducere family spreads across deduce, induce, and conduct.

latinIntro.en: Latin ducere and its compound adducere are the recorded sources.
latinIntro.cn: 记录在案的来源是拉丁语 ducere 及其复合词 adducere。

senses.title: Highly skilled at a craft

senses.definitionCN: 非常擅长需要技巧的事情
senses.example: The young watchmaker was adept at repairing tiny gears.
senses.exampleCN: 这位年轻钟表匠擅长修理细小齿轮。
senses.why: Latin adipisci meant 'to attain'; skill is what one has attained after long practice.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 adipisci 意为「达到、获得」；技艺正是长久练习后「获得」的东西。

senses.title: A person of high skill
senses.definition: a person who has attained great skill, sometimes with a hint of secret expertise
senses.definitionCN: 技艺高超之人，有时暗指深谙门道者
senses.example: Old practitioners regarded him as an adept of the trade.
senses.exampleCN: 老匠人们视他为这一行的内行。
senses.why: The noun turns attainment into a person: one who has 'arrived' at mastery.
senses.whyCN: 名词义把「已达」变成「已达之人」：抵达精通之境的人。

intro.en: Adept comes from Latin adeptus, 'attained', the participle of adipisci, 'to attain', from ad- plus sequi 'to follow after'.
intro.cn: adept 来自拉丁语 adeptus（已达成的），是 adipisci（达到）的分词，由 ad- 加 sequi（追随）构成。

items.en: The reconstructed root *sek- meant 'to follow'.
items.cn: 重构词根 *sek- 意为「跟随」。

items.en: sequi meant 'to follow'; adipisci meant 'to follow after and attain'.
items.cn: sequi 意为「跟随」；adipisci 意为「追随而达成」。

items.en: adeptus meant 'one who has attained'.
items.cn: adeptus 意为「已达成之人」。

items.en: English adept first named alchemists who claimed to have attained the secret.
items.cn: 英语 adept 最初指自称已获炼金秘术的炼金术士。

items.en: Now an ordinary word for skill; the adjective is the commonest form.
items.cn: 如今泛指技艺娴熟；形容词是最常见形式。

note.en: The first group gathers the sequi family; the second gathers words for skill and mastery.
note.cn: 第一组收 sequi 词族；第二组收表示技艺与精通的词。

entries.definition: To adjust to new conditions; only one letter apart, different root.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「适应、改编」；仅一字母之差，词源不同。

entries.definition: To take up and use; look-alike with different root.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「采纳、收养」；形近但词源不同。

entries.definition: The noun for skillfulness.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「娴熟」。

entries.definition: Having the training and ability for a task.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有技能的」。

entries.definition: Competent through practice, often with a measure attached.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「精通的」，常与程度搭配。

entries.definition: Showing the power of a master.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「高超的、老练的」。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the attain root and the adept-at pattern; the abstract hooks picture hands that never hesitate.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「达成」词根与 adept-at 句型；抽象记忆点想象毫不迟疑的手。

normal.en: Adept is adeptus: one who has attained.
normal.cn: adept 出自 adeptus：已达之人。

normal.en: Adept at is the everyday pattern; adept in is formal.
normal.cn: adept at 是日常句型；adept in 偏正式。

normal.en: Watch the triplets adapt, adopt, adept.
normal.cn: 注意三胞胎 adapt、adopt、adept。

normal.en: As a noun, an adept is a master of a craft.
normal.cn: 作名词时，adept 指一门手艺的高手。

normal.en: It once meant an alchemist who found the secret.
normal.cn: 它曾指获得秘术的炼金术士。

abstract.en: Picture hands moving through a task with zero hesitation.
abstract.cn: 想象双手做活时毫无迟疑。

abstract.en: Picture a runner reaching the summit of a skill ladder.
abstract.cn: 想象跑者登上技艺阶梯的顶端。

abstract.en: Picture a closed recipe book finally opened to its owner.
abstract.cn: 想象秘籍终于向主人翻开。

examples.en: The young watchmaker was adept at repairing tiny gears.
examples.cn: 这位年轻钟表匠擅长修理细小齿轮。

examples.en: She is adept at calming angry customers.
examples.cn: 她擅长安抚愤怒的顾客。

examples.en: Old practitioners regarded him as an adept of the trade.
examples.cn: 老匠人们视他为这一行的内行。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额代普特」——额头代代普及练出来的本领，就是熟练。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ sequi（跟随）→ adipisci（追而达成）→ adeptus（已达之人）；核心义是「追着技艺跑，直到追上」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the skill of the practiced hand, to the person who has attained mastery.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从练熟的手艺，走到已达精通之境的人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: hands that never hesitate
core.cn: 核心意象：毫不迟疑的双手

branches.en: Skill shown in smooth, sure performance.
branches.cn: 流畅笃实的表现所显示的技艺。

branches.en: The person who has attained the craft.
branches.cn: 已达精通之境的人。

branches.en: The adjective and noun are one attainment, seen and personified.
branches.cn: 形容词与名词是同一份「达成」的可见态与人化态。

branches.en: Adept at governs the everyday pattern.
branches.cn: adept at 支配日常句型。

branches.en: The alchemist past echoes in this noun sense.
branches.cn: 这个名词义里回响着炼金术士的过去。

intro.en: The word joins ad- with the follow-root seq- through the attainment participle -ept-, and its family keeps sequels and sequences.
intro.cn: 这个词经「达成」分词 -ept- 把 ad- 与「跟随」词根 seq- 结合，词族还保留 sequel 与 sequence。

latinIntro.en: Latin sequi and adipisci are the recorded ancestors.
latinIntro.cn: 记录在案的祖先是拉丁语 sequi 与 adipisci。

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「娴熟」
副词，义为「熟练地」

definition_zh: 粘附；黏合；拥护；支持
definition_en: the act of sticking firmly to a surface, or loyal support for a party or belief
core_image: 胶带贴上玻璃，撕也撕不干净
scene: 实验室里，新涂层往玻璃上一压，怎么刮都刮不掉。The new coating showed strong adhesion to glass.
sceneCN: 这里 adhesion 是「粘附、黏合」（第 1 个义项：紧贴在物体表面的性质）；句意为新涂层对玻璃表现出强黏合力。

derivatives.zh: 同根动词，义为「粘附；坚持」
同根形容词，义为「有黏性的」
同根近亲词，义为「内聚力」，指同类之间的结合

senses.title: Sticking to a surface
senses.definition: the physical state or force by which one body sticks to another
senses.definitionCN: 一个物体紧贴另一物体的状态或力
senses.example: The new coating showed strong adhesion to glass.
senses.exampleCN: 新涂层对玻璃表现出强黏合力。
senses.why: Latin haerere means 'to stick'; adhesion is the sticking that happens when something is pressed to a surface.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 haerere 意为「粘住」；adhesion 就是物体被压到表面时发生的粘着。

senses.title: Loyal support for a cause
senses.definition: agreement to join or support a party, pact, or belief
senses.definitionCN: 同意加入或支持某政党、协定或信念
senses.example: The party welcomed the adhesion of several new members.
senses.exampleCN: 该党欢迎数名新成员的加入支持。
senses.why: A mind that 'sticks' to a cause cannot be peeled away, just as glued paper cannot.
senses.whyCN: 「粘」在事业上的心撕不下来，正如粘牢的纸撕不下来。

intro.en: Adhesion comes from Latin adhaesio, 'a sticking to', from ad- 'to' plus haerere 'to stick'.
intro.cn: adhesion 来自拉丁语 adhaesio（粘着），由 ad-（向）加 haerere（粘住）构成。

items.en: The reconstructed root is often given as *(s)gher-, 'to stick, to cling'; it remains uncertain.
items.cn: 常引的重构词根 *(s)gher- 意为「粘附」；此词根尚存疑。

items.en: haerere meant 'to stick, to cling'; adhaerere meant 'to stick to'.
items.cn: haerere 意为「粘住」；adhaerere 意为「粘附于」。

items.en: adhaesio named the act or state of sticking.
items.cn: adhaesio 指粘着的行为或状态。

items.en: French adhésion brought the word into English, first in general use.
items.cn: 法语 adhésion 把该词带入英语，起初用法宽泛。

items.en: Science keeps the physical sense; the 'support' sense survives in formal writing.
items.cn: 科学领域保留物理义；「支持」义存于正式书面语。

note.en: The first group gathers the haerere family; the second gathers words for joining and holding together.
note.cn: 第一组收 haerere 词族；第二组收表示结合与聚合的词。

entries.definition: The adjective and noun for sticky substances.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词/名词，义为「有黏性的；黏合剂」。

entries.definition: A follower who sticks to a leader or creed.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「追随者、信徒」。

entries.definition: Sticking together of like parts within one body; same root, different prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「内聚力」；同根不同前缀。

entries.definition: The making of a firm join between materials.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「黏结、结合」。

entries.definition: A general word for fastening or fondness.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「附着；依恋」。

entries.definition: Faithful support, the human face of sense two.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「忠诚」，是第二义项的人文对应。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the stick root haerere and the lab scene; the abstract hooks picture tape that will not come clean.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「粘住」词根 haerere 与实验室场景；抽象记忆点想象撕不干净的胶带。

normal.en: Adhesion is ad- plus haerere: sticking to.
normal.cn: adhesion 是 ad- 加 haerere：粘附于。

normal.en: Adhesion sticks unlike things; cohesion binds like things.
normal.cn: adhesion 粘的是不同物，cohesion 聚的是同类物。

normal.en: The verb is adhere, the adjective adhesive.
normal.cn: 动词是 adhere，形容词是 adhesive。

normal.en: Give one's adhesion to is the formal support phrase.
normal.cn: give one's adhesion to 是表示拥护的正式短语。

normal.en: Coatings and glues are tested for adhesion.
normal.cn: 涂层与胶水都要测试黏着力。

abstract.en: Picture tape peeling half off and leaving glue behind.
abstract.cn: 想象胶带撕掉一半还留下残胶。

abstract.en: Picture two hands clasped and refusing to part.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手紧握不肯分开。

abstract.en: Picture a signature added at the bottom of a pact.
abstract.cn: 想象在盟约末尾添上签名。

examples.en: The new coating showed strong adhesion to glass.
examples.cn: 新涂层对玻璃表现出强黏合力。

examples.en: Poor adhesion made the wallpaper peel within a month.
examples.cn: 黏合力差让壁纸一个月内就翘起。

examples.en: The party welcomed the adhesion of several new members.
examples.cn: 该党欢迎数名新成员的加入支持。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额黑军」——额头上粘着黑漆，军队标语撕不掉，就是黏合。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ haerere（粘住）→ adhaerere → adhaesio（粘着）；核心义是「被压向表面之后，再也分不开」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from physical sticking, to the mind that sticks to a cause.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从物理上的粘着，走到粘在事业上不放的心。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: glue that will not let go
core.cn: 核心意象：撕不下来的胶

branches.en: The measured force of a glued joint.
branches.cn: 粘合处可测的力。

branches.en: The mind glued to a party or pact.
branches.cn: 粘在政党或盟约上的心。

branches.en: Both senses refuse to be peeled apart.
branches.cn: 两个义项都拒绝被撕开。

branches.en: Materials science keeps this sense at work.
branches.cn: 材料科学让这个义项始终在岗。

branches.en: Formal writing alone preserves this sense.
branches.cn: 只有正式书面语保存这个义项。

intro.en: The noun joins ad- with the stick-root haes- through the -ion ending, and the family spreads into adhere, adhesive, and cohesion.
intro.cn: 这个名词经词尾 -ion 把 ad- 与「粘住」词根 haes- 结合，词族延伸到 adhere、adhesive 与 cohesion。

latinIntro.en: Latin haerere and adhaesio are the recorded sources.
latinIntro.cn: 记录在案的来源是拉丁语 haerere 与 adhaesio。

derivatives.zh: 动词，义为「粘附；坚持」
形容词，义为「有黏性的」

definition_zh: 恳求；郑重告诫；以誓言督促
definition_en: an urgent, solemn appeal made as if under oath
core_image: 长者在病榻前握着手恳切叮嘱
scene: 老人临别前握紧女儿的手，一字一句让她答应照顾弟弟。His dying adjuration was that she never sell the farm.
sceneCN: 这里 adjuration 是「恳求、郑重告诫」（第 1 个义项：仿佛发过誓般的恳切请求）；句意为他临终恳求她永不卖掉农场。

derivatives.zh: 同根动词，义为「恳求；郑重命令」
同根近亲词，义为「发誓放弃」，方向相反

senses.title: A solemn urgent plea
senses.definition: an earnest appeal that presses the listener as if by oath
senses.definitionCN: 仿佛以誓言加身的恳切请求，逼着听者回应
senses.example: His dying adjuration was that she never sell the farm.
senses.exampleCN: 他临终恳求她永不卖掉农场。
senses.why: Latin iurare means 'to swear'; to adjure is to swear at someone, wrapping the plea in oath-weight.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 iurare 意为「发誓」；adjure 是把恳求裹上誓言的重量。

senses.title: A command backed by oath
senses.definition: a solemn command made under or with appeal to an oath
senses.definitionCN: 借助或伴随誓言发出的郑重命令
senses.example: The witness acted under adjuration to tell the whole truth.
senses.exampleCN: 证人在责令之下说出全部真相。
senses.why: When the plea hardens into duty, the appeal becomes a command the oath enforces.
senses.whyCN: 当恳求硬化为义务，请求就变成誓言所强制的命令。

intro.en: Adjuration comes from Latin adjurare, 'to swear to', from ad- 'to' plus iurare 'to swear'.
intro.cn: adjuration 来自拉丁语 adjurare（对……起誓），由 ad-（向）加 iurare（发誓）构成。

items.en: The reconstructed root *yewes- is thought to relate to sacred speech; it remains uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为重构词根 *yewes- 与神圣言辞相关；此说尚存疑。

items.en: ius meant 'law, oath'; iurare meant 'to swear'.
items.cn: ius 意为「法、誓」；iurare 意为「发誓」。

items.en: adjurare meant 'to swear to, to charge under oath'.
items.cn: adjurare 意为「对……起誓、以誓责令」。

items.en: English adjuration entered through religious and legal texts.
items.cn: 英语 adjuration 经宗教与法律文本进入。

items.en: Now rare and literary; everyday speech prefers earnest plea.
items.cn: 如今罕见而书面化；日常用语多用 earnest plea。

note.en: The first group gathers the iurare family; the second gathers words for solemn appeal.
note.cn: 第一组收 iurare 词族；第二组收表示郑重恳求的词。

entries.definition: The parent verb, to charge solemnly as if under oath.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「郑重恳求、誓令」，本词的动词形式。

entries.definition: To swear away, to renounce under oath; one letter apart, opposite direction.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「誓绝、放弃」；一字母之差，方向相反。

entries.definition: False swearing; same root with a hostile prefix.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「伪证」；同根，前缀带敌意。

entries.definition: An earnest plea without the oath element.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「恳求」，不含誓言成分。

entries.definition: Strong urging toward action.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「劝诫、勉励」。

entries.definition: A spoken curse; oath-word turned hostile.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「咒骂」，誓言词的敌意面。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the swear root iurare and the deathbed scene; the abstract hooks picture hands pressed to close a promise.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「发誓」词根 iurare 与病榻场景；抽象记忆点想象握紧的手封存承诺。

normal.en: Adjuration is ad- plus iurare: an oath pressed upon you.
normal.cn: adjuration 是 ad- 加 iurare：压到你身上的誓言。

normal.en: The verb is adjure.
normal.cn: 动词是 adjure。

normal.en: Abjure turns the oath around: to swear away.
normal.cn: abjure 把誓言反过来：发誓放弃。

normal.en: Perjury is the criminal cousin: false oath.
normal.cn: perjury 是犯罪的亲戚：假誓。

normal.en: The word is literary; use plea in speech.
normal.cn: 这个词很书面；口语用 plea。

abstract.en: Picture hands clasped tight around a promise.
abstract.cn: 想象双手紧握封存一个承诺。

abstract.en: Picture a raised hand as the plea is spoken.
abstract.cn: 想象恳求说出时举起的手。

abstract.en: Picture a will signed with a final whispered charge.
abstract.cn: 想象遗嘱签定时最后一声耳语叮嘱。

examples.en: His dying adjuration was that she never sell the farm.
examples.cn: 他临终恳求她永不卖掉农场。

examples.en: The priest's adjuration moved the crowd to silence.
examples.cn: 神父的郑重告诫让人群安静下来。

examples.en: The witness acted under adjuration to tell the whole truth.
examples.cn: 证人在责令之下说出全部真相。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额决瑞申」——额头上顶着决绝的誓言申请，就是誓令般的恳求。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ iurare（发誓）→ adjurare（以誓责令）；核心义是「把誓言的重量压在恳求上」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the oath-weighted plea, to the command that the oath enforces.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从裹着誓言的恳求，走到誓言所强制的命令。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an oath wrapped around a plea
core.cn: 核心意象：裹着誓言的恳求

branches.en: The urgent plea that weighs like an oath.
branches.cn: 重如誓言的急切恳求。

branches.en: The command the oath turns the plea into.
branches.cn: 恳求经誓言硬化成的命令。

branches.en: Both senses carry the same oath-weight.
branches.cn: 两个义项带着同一份誓言之重。

branches.en: Religious and legal texts are its native ground.
branches.cn: 宗教与法律文本是它的原生土壤。

branches.en: Both rest on iurare, the Latin verb of swearing.
branches.cn: 两者都立足拉丁语「发誓」动词 iurare。

intro.en: The noun joins ad- with the swear-root jur- through the -ation ending, and the family spreads into jury, justice, and abjure.

latinIntro.en: Latin iurare and adjurare are the recorded sources.
latinIntro.cn: 记录在案的来源是拉丁语 iurare 与 adjurare。

definition_en: a small change made to something so that it fits, works correctly, or suits a new situation

scene: 车间的老机床跑偏了，师傅停下车床，俯身去拧底座上的螺栓。He made a small adjustment to the base of the machine and the vibration stopped.
sceneCN: 这里 adjustment 是「调整动作」（第 1 个义项：为使某物更合适而做的小改动）；句意为他对机器底座做了小幅调整，震动便停止了。

pos.zh: 名词：调整；调节装置；适应；理算

senses.title: A small change made to a thing
senses.titleCN: 调整动作：对物件的小改动
senses.definition: a small change made to a device, plan, or arrangement so that it works or fits better
senses.definitionCN: 为使装置、计划或安排运转得更好或更贴合而做的小改动
senses.example: A slight adjustment to the seat made the long drive comfortable.
senses.exampleCN: 对座椅做了轻微调整，长途驾驶就舒服了。
senses.why: The core image is a tilted table leg being padded: a small turn of the bolt, and the thing sits level again.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是垫平歪斜的桌腿：螺栓只转了一点，物件便重新稳稳落地。

senses.title: A part that regulates a mechanism
senses.titleCN: 调节装置：机器上的可调部件
senses.definition: a part or mechanism used to set, tune, or regulate a machine or instrument
senses.definitionCN: 用来设定、微调或调节机器、仪器的部件或机构
senses.example: Turn the adjustment at the side of the lamp to change its angle.
senses.exampleCN: 转动灯侧面的调节装置就能改变角度。
senses.why: If the act of turning can level a thing, the part you turn becomes the adjustment itself.
senses.whyCN: 既然「拧动」能让物件归位，那么被拧动的那个部件本身也就被叫作 adjustment。

senses.title: The process of settling into a new situation
senses.titleCN: 适应过程：迁入新环境的过渡
senses.definition: the process of getting used to a new place, job, school, or set of conditions
senses.definitionCN: 逐渐熟悉新地方、新工作、新学校或新条件的过程
senses.example: Moving abroad involves a long period of adjustment.
senses.exampleCN: 移居国外需要一段很长的适应期。
senses.why: The table leg is now a person: the small changes are made inside a life until it fits its new ground.
senses.whyCN: 这里的桌腿换成了人：一点一点的改变发生在生活内部，直到它与新的地面贴合。

senses.title: Emotional adjustment
senses.titleCN: 心理调适：情绪上的重新平衡
senses.definition: the mental process of coping with stress, loss, or a changed circumstance
senses.definitionCN: 应对压力、失落或环境变化时的心理调适过程
senses.example: Counsellors help students with the emotional adjustment to college.
senses.exampleCN: 辅导员帮助学生应对进入大学后的情绪调适。
senses.why: When the thing being levelled is the mind, the change is made in feelings rather than in wood or metal.
senses.whyCN: 当被垫平的对象是心灵时，改动就发生在情绪里，而不是木头或金属里。

senses.title: Insurance loss adjustment
senses.titleCN: 保险理算：核定赔付金额
senses.definition: the assessment of an insurance claim in order to decide how much the insurer must pay
senses.definitionCN: 对保险索赔进行核定，以确定保险人应赔付多少
senses.example: The insurance adjustment reduced the claim by half.
senses.exampleCN: 保险理算把索赔金额削减了一半。
senses.why: A damaged claim is balanced against a policy: the assessor turns the figures until the two sides agree.
senses.whyCN: 受损的索赔要与保单相衡：理算员反复拨动数字，直到两边对得上。

senses.title: An official change in wages or prices
senses.definition: an official change in the level of pay, prices, or benefits, usually made at set intervals
senses.definitionCN: 对工资、价格或福利水平的正式调整，通常按固定周期进行
senses.example: The annual wage adjustment raised every salary by three percent.
senses.exampleCN: 年度工资调整把每份薪水都提高了三个百分点。
senses.why: Whole figures can be levelled too: the same small turn is applied to a rate that has drifted out of line.
senses.whyCN: 整组数字也能被垫平：同一个「拧一拧」的动作，用在已经偏离轨道的费率上。

senses.title: Calibration of an instrument
senses.definition: the act of setting an instrument or measuring device so that its readings are accurate
senses.definitionCN: 调整仪器或测量装置，使其读数重新准确的动作
senses.example: The adjustment of the scale took two careful hours.
senses.exampleCN: 校准这台天平花了两个小时，做得很仔细。
senses.why: Here the standard is accuracy itself: the instrument is turned until its pointer and the true measure coincide.
senses.whyCN: 这里的标准就是精确：仪器被反复调校，直到指针与真实量值重合。

senses.title: Adjustment to a physical condition
senses.titleCN: 对……的适应：与特定条件相合
senses.definition: in the phrase adjustment to, the process of becoming suited to a particular physical or external condition
senses.definitionCN: 用于短语 adjustment to，表示逐渐与某种身体条件或外部条件相适应的过程
senses.example: The adjustment to high altitude can cause headaches at first.
senses.exampleCN: 初到高海拔地区时，对环境的适应可能引起头痛。
senses.why: The phrase names the ground the thing must fit: adjustment to altitude, to cold, to a new rhythm.
senses.whyCN: 这个短语点明了物件必须贴合的那块地面：适应海拔、适应寒冷、适应新的作息。

intro.en: Adjustment is the noun built on adjust, a verb borrowed from Old French and usually explained through the idea of making something exact.
intro.cn: adjustment 是在动词 adjust 之上加名词后缀构成的名词；adjust 借自古法语，一般解释为「使某物变得精确、合适」。

items.en: The adverb juxta meant 'near, close by', from a root often connected with joining; the deeper origin is source uncertain.
items.cn: 副词 juxta 意为「在近旁」，其词根常被认为与「连接」有关；更早的来源不确定。

items.en: Old French adjuster, also written ajouster, meant 'to arrange, set in order'. It is usually analysed as a- plus juste 'just, exact', though a link to Latin juxta has also been proposed.
items.cn: 古法语 adjuster（也写作 ajouster）意为「安排、整理」。一般认为它由 a- 加 juste「公正、精确」构成，也有学者把它联系到拉丁语 juxta。

items.en: The verb entered English in the fourteenth or fifteenth century with the sense 'to arrange, settle, harmonize'; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 这个动词在十四或十五世纪进入英语，意为「安排、安顿、使协调」；确切的首见年代不确定。

items.en: The noun adjustment joins the verb to the French and Latin suffix -ment, which marks an act or its result.
items.cn: 名词 adjustment 由动词加法语、拉丁语来源的后缀 -ment 构成，该后缀表示动作或其结果。

items.en: The noun widened from arranging objects to adapting people, tuning machines, changing pay rates, and settling insurance claims.
items.cn: 这个名词从「整理物件」扩展到人的适应、机器的调校、工资的变动以及保险索赔的核定。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on the same adjust base; the near-meaning group gathers other words for change, fit, and measurement.
note.cn: 形近组收同一 adjust 词基构成的一族词；近义组收其他表示改变、适配与测量的词。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to change something slightly so that it fits or works better.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「调整、调节」，即小幅改变某物使其更合适或运转更好。

entries.definition: An adjective meaning able to be changed or set in different positions.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可调整的」，指能够改变或调到不同位置。

entries.definition: A noun for a person who assesses insurance claims, or a device that regulates something.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「理算员」或「调节器」，指核定索赔的人或起调节作用的装置。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to adjust again after a first change.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「重新调整」，指在第一次改动之后再次调节。

entries.definition: A noun meaning a failure to adapt to one's circumstances.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「适应不良、失调」，指未能与所处环境相适应。

entries.definition: The process of changing in order to suit a new environment; broader and often slower than an adjustment.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「适应、改编」，强调为适合新环境而改变，范围更宽、过程常更慢。

entries.definition: A change made to something, often a more deliberate and structural one.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「修改、改动」，通常指更有意为之、幅度更大的改动。

entries.definition: The exact setting of an instrument against a standard, narrower than adjustment.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「校准」，指依标准精确设定仪器，范围比 adjustment 更窄。

entries.definition: A change in form or character, with no idea of fitting or tuning.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「改变、改动」，只强调形态或性质变化，不含「调适、校准」的意思。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Old French base and the word family that grows from adjust.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的古法语词基，以及由 adjust 长出的整个词族。

normal.en: The verb adjust is borrowed from Old French, and the noun simply adds -ment.
normal.cn: 动词 adjust 借自古法语，名词只是在它后面加 -ment。

normal.en: Juste inside adjust carries exactness: to adjust is to make something exact.
normal.cn: adjust 里的 juste 带着「精确」的意思：adjust 就是把某物调到精确。

normal.en: Adjustable, adjuster and readjustment keep the same base; only the suffixes differ.
normal.cn: adjustable、adjuster、readjustment 都保留同一个词基，只是后缀不同。

normal.en: A wage adjustment changes pay, while an insurance adjustment settles a claim.
normal.cn: wage adjustment 改变的是工资，insurance adjustment 结清的是索赔。

normal.en: The phrase adjustment to always names the condition that a person or thing must fit.
normal.cn: 短语 adjustment to 总是点明人或物必须去贴合的那个条件。

abstract.en: Picture an old table with one short leg: a few turns of the bolt, and the top is level again.
abstract.cn: 想象一张旧桌子有一条短腿：螺栓转几下，桌面就重新水平了。

abstract.en: Change the table for a person in a new city: the same small turns happen inside the life.
abstract.cn: 把桌子换成一个初到新城市的人：同样的小幅转动发生在他的生活里。

abstract.en: Change it again for a scale or a salary: anything out of line can be brought back into line.
abstract.cn: 再把它换成一架天平或一份薪水：任何偏离轨道的对象都能被调回轨道。

examples.en: A slight adjustment to the seat made the whole journey pleasant.
examples.cn: 对座椅稍作调整，整段旅程就变得舒适了。

examples.en: The company announced a wage adjustment for all staff.
examples.cn: 公司宣布对所有员工进行工资调整。

examples.en: Her adjustment to the new school took most of the autumn.
examples.cn: 她花了整个秋天来适应新学校。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额贾斯特门特」——师傅蹲下身，拧一拧、垫一垫，机器就重新合身了

root: adjust 借自古法语 adjuster「安排、整理」，一般认为由 a-「向」加 juste「公正、精确」构成，juste 又来自拉丁语 justus，与 ius「权利、法」相关；也有解释把它联系到拉丁语 juxta「在近旁」。再加名词后缀 -ment 构成 adjustment。更早的印欧词根存疑。

sensesIntro.en: All eight senses apply one small act of levelling: to an object, to its regulating part, to a person settling in, to the mind, to a claim, to a rate, to an instrument, and to a specific condition.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在施加同一个「小幅归位」的动作：用在物件、调节部件、人的安顿、心理、索赔、费率、仪器，以及某个特定条件上。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a tilted leg is padded a little at a time until the whole thing stands level.
core.cn: 核心意象：歪斜的桌腿被一点一点垫平，直到整个物件重新站稳。

branches.en: THE OBJECT: a small change and the part that is turned to make it hold.
branches.cn: 物件线：一次小改动，以及被拧动的那个部件。

branches.en: THE PERSON: getting used to a place, or suiting a particular physical condition.
branches.cn: 人的线：适应一个新地方，或与某种身体条件相合。

branches.en: THE MIND: the same levelling happens in feelings rather than in wood or metal.
branches.cn: 心理线：同样的归位发生在情绪里，而不是木头或金属里。

branches.en: THE MONEY: claims and pay rates are brought back into line by the same small turns.
branches.cn: 金钱线：索赔与工资费率也靠同样的小幅拨动被调回轨道。

branches.en: THE INSTRUMENT: accuracy is the ground, and the pointer is turned until it touches it.
branches.cn: 仪器线：精确就是那块地面，指针被调到与它相接。

intro.en: Adjustment is a French borrowing dressed with Latin suffixes; the word is not built from English parts alone.
intro.cn: adjustment 是借自法语的词，再加上拉丁语来源的后缀；它并非只用英语部件构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin words behind the family are juxta, justus and ius, all recorded; only the deeper root is reconstructed.
latinIntro.cn: 这一词族背后的拉丁词 juxta、justus、ius 都有文献记录，只有更早的词根属于重构形式。

items.example: It appears in administrare and in French a-.
items.exampleCN: 它出现在拉丁语 administrare 与法语 a- 之中。

items.example: The word was taken into English as just.
items.exampleCN: 这个词被英语吸收为 just。

items.example: Adjust the mirror before you drive.

items.exampleCN: 它把 adjust 构成 adjustment。

items.example: It is the source of the idea of placing things side by side.
items.exampleCN: 它是「把事物并排放置」这一观念的来源。

definition_zh: 副官；（军队中的）人事参谋；鹳（一种鸟）
definition_en: a staff officer who helps a commander with administration; also a large stork-like bird
core_image: 站在长官身后的参谋，递文件、排班表样样在行
scene: 营部办公室里，军官把命令写好，交给身旁的助手去分发。The colonel sent the orders out through his adjutant.
sceneCN: 这里 adjutant 是「副官」（第 1 个义项：协助长官处理行政事务的参谋军官）；句意为上校经副官把命令分发出去。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「副官职务」
同根罕用词，义为「导水管；管口」

senses.title: A staff officer who assists
senses.definition: an officer who helps a commander with orders, records, and administration
senses.definitionCN: 协助指挥官处理命令、记录与行政的军官
senses.example: The colonel sent the orders out through his adjutant.
senses.exampleCN: 上校经副官把命令分发出去。
senses.why: Latin iuvare means 'to help'; the adjutant is the officer whose whole job is to help the commander.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 iuvare 意为「帮助」；adjutant 就是专门帮助指挥官的军官。

senses.title: A large stork-like bird
senses.definition: a tall Indian bird, so named as if the 'helper' of vultures at carcasses
senses.definitionCN: 印度的一种高大鸟类，因似「帮助」秃鹫拾余而得名
senses.example: The adjutant stalked the riverbank behind the feeding vultures.
senses.exampleCN: 副官鹳跟在进食的秃鹫后面沿河岸踱步。
senses.why: The bird was called the vulture's 'helper', picking up what the vultures leave.
senses.whyCN: 这种鸟被称为秃鹫的「帮手」，捡拾秃鹫吃剩的东西。

intro.en: Adjutant comes from Latin adjutare, 'to help', a frequentative of iuvare, 'to help'.
intro.cn: adjutant 来自拉丁语 adjutare（帮助），是 iuvare（帮助）的反复态。

items.en: The reconstructed root *yeu- is thought to mean 'to help'; it remains uncertain.
items.cn: 一般认为重构词根 *yeu- 意为「帮助」；此说尚存疑。

items.en: iuvare meant 'to help'; adjutare meant 'to help repeatedly'.
items.cn: iuvare 意为「帮助」；adjutare 意为「一再帮助」。

items.en: adjutans was the present participle, 'one who helps'.
items.cn: adjutans 是现在分词：「帮助者」。

items.en: English adjutant first named a military staff officer.
items.cn: 英语 adjutant 最初指军队参谋军官。

items.en: The military sense is standard; the bird name survives in natural history.
items.cn: 军义项是标准用法；鸟名留存在博物学中。

note.en: The first group gathers the iuvare family; the second gathers words for assisting roles.
note.cn: 第一组收 iuvare 词族；第二组收表示协助角色的词。

entries.definition: A rare technical word for a tube or nozzle.
entries.definitionCN: 罕用技术名词，义为「导水管、管口」。

entries.definition: The office or term of an adjutant.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「副官职务」。

entries.definition: A military helper of different Latin origin; spelling and meaning near.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「副官」；词源不同，拼写相近。

entries.definition: A personal officer assisting a general.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「随从副官」。

entries.definition: Any officer serving headquarters rather than the line.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「参谋军官」。

entries.definition: A general helper, the civilian cousin.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「助手」，是文职近亲。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the help root iuvare and the headquarters scene; the abstract hooks picture papers passed behind the commander.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「帮助」词根 iuvare 与司令部场景；抽象记忆点想象在指挥官身后传递文件。

normal.en: Adjutant is adjutare: the one who keeps helping.
normal.cn: adjutant 出自 adjutare：持续帮忙的人。

normal.en: Adjutant general is the senior staff title.
normal.cn: adjutant general 是高级参谋头衔。

normal.en: The bird name comes from playing the vulture's helper.
normal.cn: 鸟名来自它扮演秃鹫帮手。

normal.en: Aide is the French cousin with the same job.
normal.cn: aide 是干同样差事的法语近亲。

normal.en: The plural is simply adjutants.
normal.cn: 复数就是 adjutants。

abstract.en: Picture a desk where every paper passes through one hand.
abstract.cn: 想象每份文件都要经过一只手的办公桌。

abstract.en: Picture a second chair always beside the commander.
abstract.cn: 想象指挥官身旁永远摆着的第二把椅子。

abstract.en: Picture a bird trailing the clean-up crew.
abstract.cn: 想象跟在清洁队后面踱步的大鸟。

examples.en: The colonel sent the orders out through his adjutant.
examples.cn: 上校经副官把命令分发出去。

examples.en: The adjutant kept the regiment's records in perfect order.
examples.cn: 副官把团里的档案整理得井井有条。

examples.en: The adjutant stalked the riverbank behind the feeding vultures.
examples.cn: 副官鹳跟在进食的秃鹫后面沿河岸踱步。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额久他特」——长官身边久待的特别帮手，就是副官。

root: 拉丁语 iuvare（帮助）→ adjutare（一再帮助）→ adjutans（帮助者）；核心义是「长在指挥官身边的帮助之手」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from the officer who helps command, to the bird once called the vulture's helper.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从协助指挥的军官，走到曾被称作秃鹫帮手的鸟。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the helping hand always beside the commander
core.cn: 核心意象：常伴指挥官左右的帮助之手

branches.en: The officer whose trade is assistance.
branches.cn: 以协助为本职的军官。

branches.en: The bird that 'helps' the vultures.
branches.cn: 「帮助」秃鹫的鸟。

branches.en: Both names rest on the Latin idea of helping.
branches.cn: 两个名称都立足拉丁语「帮助」的观念。

branches.en: Headquarters paperwork is this sense's daily work.
branches.cn: 司令部的文书是这一义项的日常。

branches.en: Natural history keeps this sense alive.
branches.cn: 博物学让这个义项留存。

intro.en: The word carries the help-root jut- with the agent ending -ant, and the family spreads into aid and auxiliary through related verbs.
intro.cn: 这个词带着「帮助」词根 jut- 与施动词尾 -ant，词族经相关动词延伸到 aid 与 auxiliary。

latinIntro.en: Latin iuvare and adjutare are the recorded ancestors.
latinIntro.cn: 记录在案的祖先是拉丁语 iuvare 与 adjutare。

derivatives.zh: 名词，义为「副官职务」
罕用名词，义为「导水管」

definition_zh: 管理者；行政人员；遗产管理人；系统管理员
definition_en: a person who manages an organization, system or estate, or who handles its official procedures
core_image: 一个人坐在桌后，面前是三摞文件
scene: 医院走廊里，行政人员抱着文件夹快步走过，后面跟着两位医生。The administrator approved the new schedule before the ward opened.
sceneCN: 这里 administrator 是「管理者」（第 1 个义项：负责组织运营的人）；句意为这位管理者在病房开放前批准了新排班。

pos.zh: 名词：管理者；行政人员；系统管理员

derivatives.zh: 本词的动词基础，义为「管理；施行」
由动词加 -ation 构成，义为「管理；行政」
由 administration 加 -ive 构成，义为「行政的」
由本词截短的口语形式，义为「管理员」

senses.title: A manager of an organization
senses.definition: a person responsible for running the daily operations of an institution
senses.definitionCN: 负责机构日常运营的人
senses.example: The administrator met every department head on Monday.
senses.exampleCN: 管理者在周一见了每个部门的负责人。
senses.why: The -ator suffix marks the person who performs administrare, so the administrator is the one who does the serving and directing.
senses.whyCN: -ator 后缀标记执行 administrare 的人，所以 administrator 就是从事服务与指挥的那个人。

senses.title: A public administrator
senses.definition: a government official who runs public programmes and agencies
senses.definitionCN: 运营公共项目与政府机构的官员
senses.example: Public administrators must answer to elected officials.
senses.exampleCN: 公共行政官员必须对民选官员负责。
senses.why: Public business needs career managers distinct from politicians, and the word supplies that role.
senses.whyCN: 公共事务需要与政客不同的职业管理者，这个词正好提供这一角色。

senses.title: A hospital administrator
senses.definition: a person who manages the non-medical operations of a hospital, such as staffing and budgets
senses.definitionCN: 管理医院非医疗运营的人，如人员与预算
senses.example: The hospital administrator reorganized the outpatient queue.
senses.exampleCN: 医院管理者重新安排了门诊排队流程。
senses.why: Care is delivered inside a complex organization, so a manager is needed beside the clinicians.
senses.whyCN: 照护在复杂组织内部交付，所以临床人员身边需要一位管理者。

senses.title: A school administrator
senses.definition: a person who handles enrolment, discipline, records and daily school operations
senses.definitionCN: 负责招生、纪律、档案与学校日常运营的人
senses.example: The school administrator called every parent personally.
senses.exampleCN: 学校行政人员亲自给每位家长打了电话。
senses.why: Schools separate teaching from management, and the manager carries the administrative title.
senses.whyCN: 学校把教学与管理分开，管理者承担行政头衔。

senses.title: A system administrator
senses.definition: a person who maintains computers, networks and accounts in an organization
senses.definitionCN: 维护组织内计算机、网络与账户的人
senses.example: The system administrator reset every password after the breach.
senses.exampleCN: 泄露事件后，系统管理员重置了所有密码。
senses.why: Digital systems also need someone to keep accounts and permissions in order, which extends the managing role to machines.
senses.whyCN: 数字系统也需要有人维护账户与权限，这把管理角色扩展到机器。

senses.title: A database administrator
senses.definition: a specialist who controls access, backups and performance of a database
senses.definitionCN: 控制数据库访问、备份与性能的专门人员
senses.example: The database administrator restored the table from a backup.
senses.exampleCN: 数据库管理员从备份中恢复了那张表。
senses.why: Data must be governed like an office, so the word appears in a precise technical job title.
senses.whyCN: 数据必须像办公室一样被治理，所以这个词出现在精确的技术职位名中。

senses.title: An estate administrator
senses.definition: in law, a person appointed to collect, manage and distribute a deceased person's estate
senses.definitionCN: 法律上被指定收集、管理与分配死者遗产的人
senses.example: The court appointed an administrator for the estate.
senses.exampleCN: 法院为这份遗产指定了一名管理人。
senses.why: Property left behind must be accounted for, and law gives the managing person a formal name.
senses.whyCN: 留下的财产必须被核算，法律便为这位管理者给出正式名称。

senses.title: A bankruptcy administrator
senses.definition: a person appointed to manage the property and affairs of a bankrupt business or person
senses.definitionCN: 被指定管理破产企业或个人财产与事务的人
senses.example: The bankruptcy administrator sold the factory to pay creditors.
senses.exampleCN: 破产管理人卖掉工厂以偿还债权人。
senses.why: When a business fails, its remaining assets need orderly management, which is administration under legal supervision.
senses.whyCN: 企业失败时，剩余资产需要有序管理，这是法律监督下的行政。

intro.en: Administrator is the Latin agent noun of administrare, the person who serves and directs.
intro.cn: administrator 是 administrare 的拉丁施事名词，指服务并指挥的那个人。

items.en: Minus meant lesser, the root behind minister, a servant.
items.cn: minus 意为「较小」，是 minister「仆人」背后的词根。

items.en: Ad plus ministrare formed administrare, to serve, manage or carry out.
items.cn: ad 与 ministrare 构成 administrare「服务、管理、执行」。

items.en: Administrator was the recorded agent noun, the person who manages or carries out.
items.cn: administrator 是有记录的施事名词，指管理或执行的人。

items.en: Old French administrateur carried the role name into English.
items.cn: 古法语 administrateur 把这个角色名带入英语。

items.en: The English word is recorded in the fifteenth century; the exact first date is uncertain.
items.cn: 英语词在十五世纪已有记录，确切首见年代不确定。

items.en: Computing created system administrator and database administrator as precise job titles.
items.cn: 计算机领域造出 system administrator 与 database administrator 等精确职位名。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers the administer family; the near-meaning group gathers managers and officials with different authority.
note.cn: 形近组收 administer 词族；近义组收管理者与官员，权威来源不同。

entries.definition: The verb meaning to manage or give out.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「管理」或「给予」。

entries.definition: The noun for management or government.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「管理、行政、政府」。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning relating to management.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「行政的、管理的」。

entries.definition: A short informal form of administrator or administration.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「管理员、管理」，是口语缩略。

entries.definition: A rare older word for a servant or provider; it shares the same serving root.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，较旧且少见，义为「服务者、提供者」，共享同一「服务」词根。

entries.definition: A person who runs a team or business; common in commercial settings.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「经理、管理者」，常用于商业场景。

entries.definition: A senior manager with decision-making power; higher in rank than many administrators.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「高管」，拥有决策权，级别常高于一般行政人员。

entries.definition: A person holding public office; the authority comes from office, not from management.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「官员」，权威来自职位，而非管理职能。

entries.definition: A person who oversees workers; narrower and more hands-on than administrator.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「主管」，负责监督员工，范围更窄、更贴近一线。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real -ator agent suffix and the hospital, school and computing phrases the word appears in.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的 -ator 施事后缀，以及这个词实际出现的医院、学校与计算机搭配。

normal.en: The -ator ending marks the person who does the administering.
normal.cn: -ator 结尾标记执行管理工作的人。

normal.en: A system administrator manages accounts and permissions, not people.
normal.cn: 系统管理员管理的是账户与权限，而不是人。

normal.en: An estate administrator is appointed by law to settle property.
normal.cn: 遗产管理人由法律指定来处理财产。

normal.en: A public administrator runs programmes, while politicians set direction.
normal.cn: 公共行政官员运营项目，政客则设定方向。

normal.en: Admin is simply the clipped, everyday form of administrator.
normal.cn: admin 只是 administrator 的截短日常形式。

abstract.en: Picture a desk with three stacks of files and a name plate on the front edge.
abstract.cn: 想象一张桌子，三摞文件，前缘还有一块姓名牌。

abstract.en: The administrator is the person who keeps the machine oiled so others can work.
abstract.cn: 管理者是给机器上油的人，好让别人能工作。

abstract.en: Power here is procedural: it comes from keeping records straight, not from giving orders.
abstract.cn: 这里的权力是程序性的：来自把记录理清，而不是发号施令。

examples.en: The administrator signed the contract on behalf of the school.
examples.cn: 管理者代表学校签署了合同。

examples.en: Contact the system administrator if you cannot log in.
examples.cn: 如果无法登录，请联系系统管理员。

examples.en: The estate administrator distributed the property according to the will.
examples.cn: 遗产管理人按遗嘱分配了财产。
