sensesIntro.en: The eight senses all name a person who keeps an institution in order: an organization manager, public official, hospital manager, school officer, system or database keeper, estate manager, or bankruptcy manager.
sensesIntro.cn: 八个义项都在命名「让机构保持秩序的人」：组织管理者、公共官员、医院管理者、学校行政、系统或数据库维护者、遗产管理人，或破产管理人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a person behind three stacks of files with a name plate on the desk.
core.cn: 核心意象：一个人坐在三摞文件后面，桌上有姓名牌。

branches.en: THE INSTITUTION: a manager runs an organization or a school.
branches.cn: 机构线：管理者运营组织或学校。

branches.en: THE STATE: public administrators run programmes under elected officials.
branches.cn: 国家线：公共行政官员在民选官员之下运营项目。

branches.en: THE HOSPITAL: non-medical operations need their own manager.
branches.cn: 医院线：非医疗运营需要自己的管理者。

branches.en: THE MACHINE: systems and databases have named keepers.
branches.cn: 机器线：系统与数据库有具名的维护者。

branches.en: THE LAW: estates and failed businesses are placed under a manager.
branches.cn: 法律线：遗产与破产企业被置于管理人之下。

intro.en: Administrator is a Latin verb stem plus the agent suffix -ator, the person who carries out the work.

latinIntro.en: Latin administrare and administrator are recorded; the agent noun is classical.

definition_zh: 可采纳的；可接受的；（证据）有效的
definition_en: able to be accepted or allowed in, especially as evidence in court
core_image: 门口的查验员点头放行，证据得以入内
scene: 法庭上法官翻了翻笔录，示意可以呈堂。The judge ruled that the tape recording was admissible.
sceneCN: 这里 admissible 是「可采纳的」（第 1 个义项：证据可被法庭接受）；句意为法官裁定录音可采纳。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「可采纳性」
由否定前缀构成，义为「不可采纳的」
同根动词，义为「准许进入；承认」

senses.title: Allowed as evidence
senses.definition: able to be formally accepted in a court or hearing
senses.definitionCN: 可在法庭或听证中被正式接受
senses.example: The judge ruled that the tape recording was admissible.
senses.exampleCN: 法官裁定录音可采纳。
senses.why: Latin mittere means 'to send'; admissible evidence is evidence allowed to be sent into the courtroom.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 mittere 意为「送」；admissible 的证据就是被准许送进法庭的证据。

senses.title: Acceptable in a broader sense
senses.definition: reasonable enough to be accepted in argument or consideration
senses.definitionCN: 在论证或考虑中足够合理、可被接受
senses.example: Weak as it was, the excuse was admissible under the circumstances.
senses.exampleCN: 尽管牵强，这个借口在当时情形下还算说得过去。
senses.why: The door of admission opens figuratively: the argument is let in, though not yet endorsed.
senses.whyCN: 「入门」之门被比喻地打开：论证被放进来，虽未获认可。

intro.en: Admissible joins Latin ad- 'to' with missio's verb mittere 'to send', through the -ible ending 'able to be'.
intro.cn: admissible 把拉丁语 ad-（向）与 mittere（送）经 -ible（可……的）词尾结合。

items.en: The reconstructed root *meyth- meant 'to swap, to move'; it remains uncertain.
items.cn: 重构词根 *meyth- 意为「交换、移动」；此词根尚存疑。

items.en: mittere meant 'to send, to let go'; admittere meant 'to let in'.
items.cn: mittere 意为「送出、放走」；admittere 意为「准许进入」。

items.en: admissibilis meant 'that may be let in'.
items.cn: admissibilis 意为「可被放入的」。

items.en: English admissible settled first in law, then widened.
items.cn: 英语 admissible 先在法律中定着，后扩展。

items.en: Legal use dominates; inadmissible is equally common.
items.cn: 法律用法占主导；inadmissible 同样常见。

note.en: The first group gathers the mittere family; the second gathers words for acceptable status.
note.cn: 第一组收 mittere 词族；第二组收表示可接受状态的词。

entries.definition: The noun for whether evidence may come in.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「可采纳性」。

entries.definition: The negated form, barred from acceptance.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「不可采纳的」。

entries.definition: The act of letting in, or of acknowledging.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「进入许可；承认」。

entries.definition: Good enough to be taken.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可接受的」。

entries.definition: Permitted by rules.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「允许的」。

entries.definition: Legally sound and effective.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「有效的」。

normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「送」词根 mittere 与法庭场景；抽象记忆点想象守门人点头放行证据。

normal.en: Admissible is admit plus -ible: able to be let in.
normal.cn: admissible 是 admit 加 -ible：可被放入的。

normal.en: Admissible evidence is the core legal collocation.
normal.cn: admissible evidence 是核心法律搭配。

normal.en: Inadmissible flips it: barred at the door.
normal.cn: inadmissible 反其道：门口拦下。

normal.en: The noun is admissibility.
normal.cn: 名词是 admissibility。

normal.en: The same root gives admit, mission, and permit.
normal.cn: 同一词根产出 admit、mission 与 permit。

abstract.en: Picture a guard checking papers and waving one through.
abstract.cn: 想象守卫查验证件后放行一份。

abstract.en: Picture evidence slipping past the courtroom door.
abstract.cn: 想象证据溜进法庭的门。

abstract.en: Picture a stamp that says 'accepted' on a folder.
abstract.cn: 想象文件夹上盖上「已受理」的章。

examples.en: The judge ruled that the tape recording was admissible.
examples.cn: 法官裁定录音可采纳。

examples.en: Hearsay is generally not admissible in criminal trials.
examples.cn: 刑事审判中传闻证据一般不可采纳。

examples.en: Weak as it was, the excuse was admissible under the circumstances.
examples.cn: 尽管牵强，这个借口在当时情形下还算说得过去。

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from evidence formally let into court, to arguments informally let into discussion.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从被正式放进法庭的证据，走到被非正式放进讨论的论证。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a gatekeeper waving the evidence in
core.cn: 核心意象：守门人放行证据

branches.en: Evidence that passes the courtroom door.
branches.cn: 通过法庭之门的证据。

branches.en: An argument merely allowed into the talk.
branches.cn: 仅被允许进入讨论的论证。

branches.en: Both senses are 'let in', one formal, one loose.
branches.cn: 两个义项都是「放进来」，一正式一宽松。

branches.en: Law is the home ground of this sense.
branches.cn: 法律是这个义项的主场。

branches.en: Both stand on mittere, the Latin verb of sending.
branches.cn: 两者都立足拉丁语「送」动词 mittere。

definition_zh: 进入权；准入；（电路的）导纳
definition_en: permission or the right to enter a place; in electrical engineering, a measure of how easily current enters a circuit
core_image: 写着「闲人免进」的门禁，刷卡才放行
scene: 机房门口挂着警示牌，值班员刷了卡，门才缓缓开锁。Only staff with badges are granted admittance to the control room.
sceneCN: 这里 admittance 是「进入权、准入」（第 1 个义项：获准进入某处的许可）；句意为只有持证员工获准进入控制室。

derivatives.zh: 同根动词，义为「准许进入；承认」

senses.title: The right to enter
senses.definition: permission to go into a place, often shown by a sign or a pass
senses.definitionCN: 进入某处的许可，常以标牌或通行证体现
senses.example: Only staff with badges are granted admittance to the control room.
senses.exampleCN: 只有持证员工获准进入控制室。
senses.why: Latin mittere means 'to send'; admittance is the state of being sent in through a door.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 mittere 意为「送」；admittance 就是被送进门的状态。

senses.title: Electrical admittance
senses.definition: a technical measure of how easily alternating current flows into a circuit
senses.definitionCN: 衡量交流电流入电路难易程度的技术量
senses.example: The engineer measured the admittance of the antenna circuit.
senses.exampleCN: 工程师测量了天线电路的导纳。
senses.why: Current, like a visitor, is 'sent in' through the circuit; admittance names how easily the door opens.
senses.whyCN: 电流如访客般被「送入」电路；admittance 命名的是这扇门有多容易打开。

intro.en: Admittance is admit plus -ance, from Latin admittere, 'to let in', from ad- plus mittere, 'to send'.
intro.cn: admittance 由 admit 加 -ance 构成，源自拉丁语 admittere（准许进入），由 ad- 加 mittere（送）构成。

items.en: The reconstructed root *meyth- meant 'to swap, to move'; it remains uncertain.

items.en: mittere meant 'to send'; admittere meant 'to let in'.
items.cn: mittere 意为「送」；admittere 意为「准许进入」。

items.en: English admittance grew beside admission, both meaning the act of letting in.
items.cn: 英语 admittance 与 admission 并行发展，均指准许进入的行为。

items.en: No admittance signs fixed the word on doors; engineers later borrowed it for circuits.
items.cn: 「禁止入内」标牌把这个词钉在了门上；工程师后来把它借给电路。

items.en: Everyday use centres on signs and passes; admission is commoner for tickets.
items.cn: 日常用法集中于标牌与通行证；门票语境更常用 admission。

senses.title: To warn someone firmly
senses.definition: to warn someone strongly about a danger or a likely mistake, so that they avoid it
senses.definitionCN: 就某种危险或可能的错误强烈提醒某人，使其避开
senses.example: The guide admonished us not to swim beyond the reef.
senses.exampleCN: 向导告诫我们不要游到礁石之外。
senses.why: The word carries a reminder that comes as a tap on the shoulder: the warning arrives before the harm, not after.
senses.whyCN: 这个词带着「肩头被轻敲一下」的提醒：警告在伤害之前到达，而不是之后。

senses.title: To rebuke mildly
senses.definition: to criticize someone for a fault in a quiet, corrective way rather than with anger
senses.definitionCN: 以平静、纠正性的方式批评某人的过失，而不是发怒
senses.example: The teacher admonished the boy for talking during the test.
senses.exampleCN: 老师责备那个男孩考试时讲话。
senses.why: A rebuke here is still a reminder: the fault is named so that it will not be repeated, not to humiliate.
senses.whyCN: 这里的责备仍是一种提醒：指出过失是为了不再重犯，而不是为了羞辱。

senses.title: To remind someone of a duty
senses.definition: to remind a person of a responsibility or an obligation they must not forget
senses.definitionCN: 提醒某人不要忘记某项责任或义务
senses.example: The judge admonished the jury to weigh the evidence carefully.
senses.exampleCN: 法官提醒陪审团仔细权衡证据。
senses.why: The oldest layer of the word is simply to put something into someone's mind, and a duty is exactly what must be kept there.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最古老的一层就是「把事情放进某人心里」，而职责正是必须一直放在那里的东西。

senses.title: To urge earnestly
senses.definition: to urge someone seriously to do or avoid something, often in a formal setting
senses.definitionCN: 郑重敦促某人去做或避免某事，常用于正式场合
senses.example: The doctor admonished him to rest for a full week.
senses.exampleCN: 医生郑重劝他休息整整一周。
senses.why: Urging is a warning turned forward: instead of describing the danger, the speaker presses a course of action on the listener.
senses.whyCN: 敦促是把警告转向前方：说话者不再描述危险，而是把某个做法压到听者身上。

senses.title: To counsel morally
senses.definition: to give moral or religious counsel, often from a position of authority
senses.definitionCN: 从权威位置给出道德或宗教上的训导
senses.example: The elder admonished the young men to keep their promises.
senses.exampleCN: 长者训诫年轻人要守信。
senses.why: Authority gives the reminder weight: the same words from a stranger would be advice, but from an elder they are a charge.
senses.whyCN: 权威给提醒增加了分量：同样的话出自陌生人之口只是建议，出自长者之口便成了训诫。

senses.title: To caution against a consequence
senses.definition: to point out the bad consequence that will follow if a warning is ignored
senses.definitionCN: 指出若无视警告将会出现的坏后果
senses.example: The inspector admonished the company against ignoring the safety rules.
senses.exampleCN: 检查员警告该公司不要无视安全规定。
senses.why: The reminder is paired with a forecast: the door is still open, but the speaker describes what lies behind it.
senses.whyCN: 提醒配上了一个预报：门还开着，但说话者描述门后有什么。

senses.title: To issue an official reprimand
senses.definition: to record a formal reprimand, especially in law, employment, or a disciplinary process
senses.definitionCN: 记录正式申诫，多用于法律、雇佣或纪律程序
senses.example: The court admonished the witness for refusing to answer.
senses.exampleCN: 法庭就证人拒答一事对其予以申诫。
senses.why: Once the reminder is written down, a private tap becomes a public record, and the word enters official language.
senses.whyCN: 提醒一旦被写下来，私下的一记轻敲就变成公开记录，这个词也由此进入官方语言。

senses.title: To urge someone to do something
senses.definition: to press someone to carry out an action, in the pattern admonish someone to do something
senses.definitionCN: 以 admonish someone to do something 的结构催促某人采取行动
senses.example: She admonished her brother to call their mother more often.
senses.exampleCN: 她敦促弟弟多给母亲打电话。
senses.why: The reminder has a target: it is not only about what to avoid, but about the act that should now be performed.
senses.whyCN: 提醒有了目标：不只是要避开什么，还包括现在就应该去做的那件事。

intro.en: Admonish comes from a Latin verb of reminding, and its family is full of words about warning, memory and advice.
intro.cn: admonish 来自一个表示「提醒」的拉丁动词，它的词族里满是与警告、记忆和建议有关的词。

items.en: The warning root is often connected with *men-, 'to think, mind', but the reconstruction is not certain.
items.cn: 这个「警告」词根常与 *men-「思考、心智」联系起来，但构拟并不确定。

items.en: Monere meant 'to warn, remind, advise', and it also produced monitor and monument.
items.cn: monere 意为「警告、提醒、建议」，它还生出 monitor 与 monument。

items.en: Ad plus monere formed admonere, 'to remind, warn, urge'. The prefix adds direction rather than intensity.
items.cn: ad 与 monere 构成 admonere，意为「提醒、警告、敦促」。前缀加的是方向，而不是强度。

items.en: Old French amonester carried the word into English, where the Latin d was restored by later spelling.
items.cn: 古法语 amonester 把词带入英语，后来的拼写又恢复了拉丁语的 d。

items.en: The verb appears in the fourteenth century with the senses of warning, advising and reproving already together.
items.cn: 动词于十四世纪出现，警告、建议与责备三个义项当时已经并存。

items.en: Legal and workplace usage adds a formal reprimand, while everyday usage keeps the quiet corrective tone.
items.cn: 法律与职场用法增加了正式申诫一义，日常用法则保留平静纠正的语气。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers words from the same Latin warning root; the near-meaning group gathers verbs of warning and criticism, which differ in force and in who has the authority to speak.
note.cn: 形近组收同一拉丁「警告」词根构成的词；近义组收警告与批评类动词，彼此在力度和说话者权威上不同。

entries.definition: The noun for a warning or a mild rebuke.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「告诫、温和的责备」。

entries.definition: The adjective meaning serving as a warning.

entries.definition: The noun for the act or result of admonishing.

entries.definitionCN: 同词根的名词或动词，现代义偏向「监测」而不是「纠正」。

entries.definition: To tell someone about a danger so that they can avoid it, without implying a fault.
entries.definitionCN: 告知危险以便对方避开，不暗示对方已有过失，语气更中性。

entries.definition: To criticize someone sharply because they have done something wrong.
entries.definitionCN: 因对方做错事而尖锐批评，力度比 admonish 强。

entries.definition: To give an official or formal scolding, especially in work or the armed forces.
entries.definitionCN: 给予正式或官方的斥责，多用于职场或军队。

entries.definition: To advise someone to be careful, usually before any fault has occurred.
entries.definitionCN: 建议对方小心，通常发生在过失之前，强调预防。

normalIntro.en: These hooks use the real Latin warning root and the patterns the verb actually takes.
normalIntro.cn: 下面这些记忆钩子使用真实的拉丁「警告」词根，以及这个动词实际采用的句型。

normal.en: monere means to warn or remind: admonish is a warning aimed at a particular person.
normal.cn: monere 意为「警告、提醒」：admonish 就是对准某个人的警告。

normal.en: The same root gives monitor and monument, both about keeping something in mind.
normal.cn: 同一词根给出 monitor 与 monument，两者都与「把某事记在心里」有关。

normal.en: Admonish someone for a fault, and admonish someone against a danger.
normal.cn: 因过失用 admonish someone for，针对危险用 admonish someone against。

normal.en: The -ish here is not the English suffix meaning like; it came from an Old French verb ending.
normal.cn: 这里的 -ish 不是英语中表示「像……」的后缀，它来自古法语动词词尾。

normal.en: Admonish keeps a quiet tone: it corrects without shouting.
normal.cn: admonish 保持平静的语气：它纠正人，但不喊叫。

abstract.en: Picture a hand tapping a shoulder just before a step is taken, not after the fall.
abstract.cn: 想象一只的手在迈步之前轻拍肩膀，而不是在摔倒之后。

abstract.en: The tap is the same whether it warns, reminds or reproves: someone is being steered back to the right line.
abstract.cn: 这记轻拍无论是警告、提醒还是责备都一样：有人在被引回正确的线上。

abstract.en: A written admonition is that tap turned into ink, which is why courts and employers can use it.
abstract.cn: 书面的 admonition 就是那记轻拍变成了墨迹，所以法庭和雇主都能使用它。

examples.en: The ranger admonished the hikers to carry enough water.
examples.cn: 护林员告诫徒步者要带够水。

examples.en: She was admonished for leaving the laboratory unlocked.
examples.cn: 她因没锁实验室的门而受到责备。

examples.en: His letter admonished the committee against a hasty decision.
examples.cn: 他的信告诫委员会不要仓促作出决定。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（朝向）+ monere（警告、提醒）构成 admonere，字面为「对着某人提醒」，故有告诫、劝告与温和责备三义。

sensesIntro.en: Eight senses of admonish all deliver the same reminder in different settings: a danger to avoid, a fault to correct, a duty to keep, a course to follow, a moral charge, a consequence, an official record, or an act to perform.
sensesIntro.cn: admonish 的八个义项都在不同场合递出同一份提醒：要避开的危险、要纠正的过失、要记住的职责、要遵循的做法、道德上的训导、不良后果、官方记录，或应当去做的事。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand taps a shoulder at the edge of a wrong step and points back to the right line.
core.cn: 核心意象：在即将迈错的一步边上，一只手轻拍肩膀，把人指回正确的线。

branches.en: THE DANGER LINE: the reminder arrives before harm and describes what waits if it is ignored.
branches.cn: 危险线：提醒在伤害之前到达，并说明若被无视会有什么等着。

branches.en: THE FAULT LINE: a fault already committed is named calmly so that it is not repeated.
branches.cn: 过失线：已经犯下的过失被平静地点出，为的是不再重犯。

branches.en: THE DUTY LINE: authority keeps a responsibility or a moral charge in the listener's mind.
branches.cn: 职责线：权威把某项责任或道德训导留在听者心里。

branches.en: THE ACTION LINE: the warning turns forward and presses a particular act on the listener.
branches.cn: 行动线：警告转向前方，把某个具体行动压到听者身上。

branches.en: THE RECORD LINE: the private tap becomes a written reprimand inside an institution.
branches.cn: 记录线：私下的一记轻敲变成机构内部的书面申诫。

intro.en: Admonish is a Latin prefix plus a Latin warning verb, with an Old French verb ending; English adds the noun and adjective suffixes.
intro.cn: admonish 由拉丁语前缀、拉丁「警告」动词和古法语动词词尾构成；英语再加入名词与形容词后缀。

latinIntro.en: Monere, admonere and admonitio are recorded in Latin, so no part of the core is reconstructed except the deeper Indo-European root.
latinIntro.cn: monere、admonere 与 admonitio 在拉丁语中都有记录，除更早的印欧词根外，核心部分都不属重构。

intro.cn: 这个名词把 admonish 与行为后缀 -ition 结合，monere 词族延伸到 monitor、monument 与 premonition。

latinIntro.en: Latin monere, admonere, and admonitio are the recorded sources.
latinIntro.cn: 记录在案的来源是拉丁语 monere、admonere 与 admonitio。

derivatives.zh: 动词，义为「告诫」
形容词，义为「告诫性的」

definition_zh: 崇拜；爱慕；敬慕
definition_en: deep love, worship, or admiration shown openly
core_image: 台下屏息仰望着台上的人，眼里全是光
scene: 演唱会散场，歌迷围着栏杆不肯走，喊着偶像的名字。The young pianist accepted the crowd's adoration with a deep bow.
sceneCN: 这里 adoration 是「爱慕、崇拜」（第 1 个义项：公开表露的深爱或敬意）；句意为年轻钢琴家深深鞠躬接受观众的爱慕。

derivatives.zh: 同根动词，义为「崇拜；热爱」
同根形容词，义为「可爱的；值得崇拜的」

senses.title: Deep love and admiration
senses.definition: strong affection or admiration expressed openly toward a person or thing
senses.definitionCN: 对人或事物公开表露的强烈热爱与倾慕
senses.example: The young pianist accepted the crowd's adoration with a deep bow.
senses.exampleCN: 年轻钢琴家深深鞠躬接受观众的爱慕。
senses.why: Latin orare means 'to speak, to pray'; adoration is the heart turned fully toward what it speaks to.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 orare 意为「说、祈祷」；adoration 是心完全朝向它所诉说的对象。

senses.title: Worship offered to God
senses.definition: reverent worship given to a deity
senses.definitionCN: 献给神明的虔敬崇拜
senses.example: The hymn is an act of adoration at the close of the service.
senses.exampleCN: 这首圣歌是礼拜结束时的一次敬拜。
senses.why: The praying mouth is the oldest image: worship is speech offered upward.
senses.whyCN: 祈祷之口是最古老的意象：敬拜就是向上呈递的话语。

intro.en: Adoration comes from Latin adoratio, 'a speaking to, a worship', from adorare 'to worship', from ad- plus orare 'to speak, to pray'.
intro.cn: adoration 来自拉丁语 adoratio（诉说、崇拜），出自 adorare（敬拜），由 ad- 加 orare（说、祈祷）构成。

items.en: The reconstructed root *or- meant 'to speak, to pronounce'; it remains uncertain.
items.cn: 重构词根 *or- 意为「说、念出」；此词根尚存疑。

items.en: orare meant 'to speak, to pray'; adorare meant 'to speak to in worship'.
items.cn: orare 意为「说、祈祷」；adorare 意为「向……祈祷敬拜」。

items.en: adoratio named the act of worship.
items.cn: adoratio 指敬拜行为。

items.en: English adoration came through French, first religious, then romantic.
items.cn: 英语 adoration 经法语进入，先指宗教敬拜，后转情爱。

items.en: Now both romantic and religious uses are alive; adorable drove a new popular branch.
items.cn: 如今情爱与宗教两义并存；adorable 带出新的流行分支。

note.en: The first group gathers the orare family; the second gathers words for worship and love.
note.cn: 第一组收 orare 词族；第二组收表示崇拜与热爱的词。

entries.definition: The adjective for lovable, in daily speech.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「可爱的」，日常高频。

entries.definition: The verb of loving deeply.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「崇拜、热爱」。

entries.definition: A formal speech; same root turned rhetorical.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「演说」；同根转向修辞义。

entries.definition: Reverent devotion to a deity.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「敬拜」。

entries.definition: Loyal love and dedication.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「忠诚热爱；奉献」。

entries.definition: Deep respect for what is revered.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「崇敬」，敬意更庄重。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the pray root orare and the concert scene; the abstract hooks picture eyes full of light.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用「祈祷」词根 orare 与演唱会场景；抽象记忆点想象盛满光的眼睛。

normal.en: Adoration is adore plus -ation.
normal.cn: adoration 是 adore 加 -ation。

normal.en: It is stronger than liking: it is worship-grade love.
normal.cn: 它强于喜欢：是崇拜级的爱。

normal.en: Oration and oracle share the speak root.
normal.cn: oration 与 oracle 同用「说」词根。

normal.en: Religious use keeps it formal.
normal.cn: 宗教用法让它保持庄重。

normal.en: Adorable is its everyday cousin.
normal.cn: adorable 是它的日常近亲。

abstract.en: Picture fans pressing at the stage rail, shouting one name.
abstract.cn: 想象歌迷挤在舞台栏杆边呼喊同一个名字。

abstract.en: Picture hands folded upward in a quiet chapel.
abstract.cn: 想象小教堂里向上合拢的手。

abstract.en: Picture a bow that returns a sea of applause.
abstract.cn: 想象以一鞠躬回应满场掌声。

examples.en: The young pianist accepted the crowd's adoration with a deep bow.
examples.cn: 年轻钢琴家深深鞠躬接受观众的爱慕。

examples.en: He looked at her with open adoration.
examples.cn: 他毫不掩饰地满眼爱慕地看着她。

examples.en: The hymn is an act of adoration at the close of the service.
examples.cn: 这首圣歌是礼拜结束时的一次敬拜。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额道雷申」——额头上写满崇拜道别雷鸣般的掌声，就是爱慕。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ orare（说、祈祷）→ adorare（敬拜）→ adoratio（崇拜）；核心义是「把心与话完全朝向所爱」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from open admiration of a person, to reverent worship of God.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从对人的公开倾慕，走到对神的虔敬敬拜。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: eyes full of light turned upward
core.cn: 核心意象：向上仰望的盛满光的眼睛

branches.en: The open love shown to a person.
branches.cn: 对一个人公开表露的爱。

branches.en: The worship offered upward to God.
branches.cn: 向上献给神的敬拜。

branches.en: Both senses are a heart turned fully toward its object.
branches.cn: 两个义项都是完全朝向对象的心。

branches.en: Fans and lovers live in this sense.
branches.cn: 歌迷与恋人栖居这个义项。

branches.en: Liturgy keeps this sense solemn.
branches.cn: 礼仪让这个义项保持庄严。

intro.en: The noun joins adore with the act suffix -ation, and the orare family spreads into oracle, oration, and inexorable.
intro.cn: 这个名词把 adore 与行为后缀 -ation 结合，orare 词族延伸到 oracle、oration 与 inexorable。

latinIntro.en: Latin orare, adorare, and adoratio are the recorded sources.
latinIntro.cn: 记录在案的来源是拉丁语 orare、adorare 与 adoratio。

not to be moved by plea

derivatives.zh: 动词，义为「崇拜」
形容词，义为「可爱的」

definition_zh: 装饰；装扮；使增色
definition_en: to add something beautiful or decorative to a person or thing, or to make something more attractive
core_image: 给圣诞树一盏一盏挂上彩灯，树越挂越亮
scene: 圣诞前夜，全家围着树把祖传的玻璃球一枚一枚挂上去。The children adorned the Christmas tree with glass balls.
sceneCN: 这里 adorn 是「装饰」（第 1 个义项：给某物添上美丽之物）；句意为孩子们用玻璃球装饰圣诞树。

derivatives.zh: 由本词加名词后缀构成，义为「装饰品；装点」
由本词过去分词构成，义为「装饰过的；饰有的」

senses.title: To decorate a thing
senses.definition: to add ornaments or beautiful details to an object or place
senses.definitionCN: 给物品或场所添加饰品或美的细节
senses.example: The children adorned the Christmas tree with glass balls.
senses.exampleCN: 孩子们用玻璃球装饰圣诞树。
senses.why: Latin ornare means 'to equip, to fit out'; adding beauty is a way of furnishing a thing to its best.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁语 ornare 意为「装备、配置」；添上美丽就是给物件配上它最好的样子。

senses.title: To add beauty to a person
senses.definition: to make a person more beautiful with clothes or jewels, or to lend grace to a scene or name
senses.definitionCN: 用衣着首饰使某人更美，或给场面、名字增添光彩
senses.example: She wore the jade bracelet that adorned her wrist at every feast.
senses.exampleCN: 每次宴席她都戴上那只为手腕增色的玉镯。
senses.why: The same furnishing sense turns on the person: to adorn is to dress someone so the beauty is completed.
senses.whyCN: 同一「配置」之义落到人身上：装扮某人，让美得以完成。

intro.en: Adorn comes from Latin adornare, 'to equip, to decorate', from ad- 'to' plus ornare 'to equip, to adorn', the root of ornament.
intro.cn: adorn 来自拉丁语 adornare（装备、装饰），由 ad-（向）加 ornare（装备、装饰）构成，ornament 同根。

items.en: The reconstructed root behind ornare relates to order and fitting arrangement.
items.cn: ornare 背后的重构词根与「秩序、妥帖的安排」相关。

items.en: ornare meant 'to equip, to fit out, to embellish'.
items.cn: ornare 意为「装备、配置、修饰」。

items.en: adornare added ad-, so the furnishing was pressed onto the thing.
items.cn: adornare 加上 ad-，把「配置」压到物件身上。

items.en: French adorner carried the word toward English.
items.cn: 法语 adorner 把这个词带向英语。

items.en: English adorn keeps the literary tone: walls, temples, and wrists are adorned.
items.cn: 英语 adorn 保留书面色彩：墙壁、殿堂与手腕都可被 adorn。

note.en: The first group gathers the ornare family; the second gathers verbs of decorating and dressing up.
note.cn: 第一组收 ornare 词族；第二组收表示装饰、装扮的动词。

entries.definition: The noun for an ornament or the act of decorating.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「装饰品；装点」。

entries.definition: A decorative object; the noun cousin of adorn.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「装饰品」，与 adorn 同根。

entries.definition: An adjective for heavy, elaborate decoration.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「装饰繁复的」。

entries.definition: The everyday verb for making a place look festive or fine.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「装饰」，日常用词。

entries.definition: To add beautiful details, sometimes also to a story.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「润饰；添枝加叶」。

entries.definition: A literary verb meaning to dress up, as in deck the halls.
entries.definitionCN: 动词，义为「装点」，如 deck the halls，偏文学。

normalIntro.en: The normal hooks use the ornare root and the ornament noun; the abstract hooks picture lights going up on a tree.
normalIntro.cn: 常规记忆点用 ornare 词根与 ornament 名词；抽象记忆点想象彩灯一盏盏挂上树。

normal.en: Adorn is ornament as a verb: same root ornare.
normal.cn: adorn 是动词版的 ornament：同根 ornare。

normal.en: Be adorned with is the standard passive pattern.
normal.cn: be adorned with 是标准被动结构。

normal.en: The noun is adornment, the adjective-leaning form is ornate.
normal.cn: 名词是 adornment，形容词一脉是 ornate。

normal.en: Adorn is more literary than decorate.
normal.cn: adorn 比 decorate 更书面。

normal.en: People as well as things can be adorned.
normal.cn: 人和物都可被 adorn。

abstract.en: Picture glass balls going onto a tree one by one.
abstract.cn: 想象玻璃球一枚枚挂上圣诞树。

abstract.en: Picture a temple doorway carved until it glows.
abstract.cn: 想象庙门被雕到发亮。

abstract.en: Picture a bracelet settling on a wrist at a feast.
abstract.cn: 想象宴席上手镯落定在腕间。

examples.en: The children adorned the Christmas tree with glass balls.
examples.cn: 孩子们用玻璃球装饰圣诞树。

examples.en: The walls were adorned with portraits of past mayors.
examples.cn: 墙上挂满了历任市长的肖像。

examples.en: Her wit adorned every conversation she joined.
examples.cn: 她的机智为每一次交谈增色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「额到恩」——额前挂到成串的饰品，恩宠加身，就是装扮。

root: 拉丁语 ad-（向）+ ornare（装备、修饰）→ adornare（装饰）；核心义是「把美丽配置到人或物上」

sensesIntro.en: The senses move from decorating a thing, to lending beauty or grace to a person or a moment.
sensesIntro.cn: 这些义项从装点物件，走到为人或时刻增添光彩。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: lights hung one by one on a tree
core.cn: 核心意象：彩灯一盏盏挂上树

branches.en: Ornaments added to an object or a place.
branches.cn: 给物品或场所添上饰品。

branches.en: Beauty added to a person or a scene.
branches.cn: 为人或场面增添美。

branches.en: Both senses furnish the subject with beauty.
branches.cn: 两个义项都在给对象配置美丽。

branches.en: Temples and halls are its literary home ground.
branches.cn: 殿堂与大厅是它的书面主场。

branches.en: Both rest on Latin ornare, to equip and embellish.
branches.cn: 两者都立足拉丁语 ornare：装备并修饰。

intro.en: The verb joins the Latin prefix ad- with the root orn-, and the family adds the noun, adjective, and agent forms.
intro.cn: 这个词把拉丁语前缀 ad- 与词根 orn- 结合，词族另加名词与形容词形式。

latinIntro.en: Latin ornare and adornare are the recorded sources.
latinIntro.cn: 记录在案的来源是拉丁语 ornare 与 adornare。

to fit up, to instigate secretly
